Chapter Notes

I was a little nervous about including Cyrene in this since we don't know much about her yet, but hopefully she feels in character! At any rate I'm sleep-deprived again so I have fewer inhibitions about posting

Also these chapters keep getting longer when I meant to keep them short... Hopefully it's a good kind of length though!

In spite of his many setbacks, Anaxa had apparently managed to reach an epiphany in record time, and within the next week, Phainon’s treatment officially begins.

It’s been two weeks since then. Mydei can’t be beside him at every session, a fact that pains him. However, Okhema’s repairs are also coming along smoothly, leaving him with more free time than before. Finding himself blissfully unoccupied one afternoon, he decides to head to the Garden of Life, where he was told Phainon is currently resting. As he nears, he hears a child’s humming, and upon emerging from the elevator, he sees Phainon sitting in the shade of the largest tree, with Tribbie and Trianne weaving flowers together, and Trinnon perched on a seat nearby, singing a soft melody. Upon his approach, Trianne raises her head, and her expression brightens.

“Look, it’s De!”

“Shh, Trianne, don’t be so loud!” Tribbie chides. “Naxy said we should stay quiet around Snowy so we don’t disturb him while he’s resting.”

“Oh! Whoops…”

Mydei manages a muted smile at the innocent sight. “Have you been taking care of him?”

“Mmhm! Snowy’s treatment started, so he must be really tired! Naxy and Cinny may be gentle, but doctor’s appointments are always scary for everyone. Even Naxy said he might be under a lot of stress, even if he doesn’t show it,” Trianne says. “Snowy needs a lot of rest in general, after everything he’s been through… That’s why we want to help him relax. So we always try to spend time with him after every treatment!”

“Whenever Snowy got anxious as a child, we would sing songs for him to calm him down. He seemed to like them, especially the ones Trianne sang,” Tribbie explains. “But Trianne’s been singing for him a lot, so we’re giving her vocal chords a break today. This time, it’s Trinnon’s turn.”

Trinnon pauses her humming briefly to add, “We hope that Snowy still likes our songs, even now. Even if he may not remember them anymore.”

“I’m sure he does,” Mydei replies. “He would never forget something so meaningful.”

The three exchange a smile before looking back at the former crown prince. “Would you like to stay with us too, De?” Tribbie asks.

“If you don’t mind.”

“Not at all! Snowy loves you, so he’ll relax even more if you’re here!”

Mydei allows himself a small chuckle. If Phainon were at his prime, he’d be doing anything but relaxing in Mydei’s presence. Closing his eyes, Mydei can imagine it now—upon seeing him, Phainon would leap up from his chair and immediately challenge him to whatever nonsensical duel he had been brewing in his mind. And Mydei, never one to refuse a challenge, would accept, and they’d lose themselves in the spirit of competition, at least until Aglaea caught wind of their shenanigans and scolded them.

When Mydei opens his eyes, he almost expects that to be the sight that greets him. But instead, Phainon remains doll-like and still, not even reacting to his rival’s presence. Feeling a powerful ache in his chest, one that has become far too familiar ever since the world had been restored, Mydei sighs softly and walks over to join Phainon in the shade, finding a spot against the tree trunk to lean on. Rather than mull over his dispiriting thoughts, he decides to observe Tribbie and Trianne instead. Tribbie is still in the middle of her flower crown, but Trianne has finished hers, holding it up proudly for Mydei to see.

“It’s done!” she declares. “De, look! We chose all of Snowy’s favourite colours today. They’ll look really good in his white hair, don’t you think?”

“...Ha. Impressive. Somehow, you managed to coordinate the colours perfectly. Had the task been left in Phainon’s hands, he surely would have made this combination look utterly garish,” Mydei replies with a small smile. “He could stand to learn a thing or two from you.”

Basking in Mydei’s praise, Trianne flashes a toothy grin, then flutters behind Phainon’s head to crown him. “Okay! Trianne’s gonna put it on now!”

However, Tribbie looks more doubtful, flitting over to examine the crown as well. “Are you sure it’s ready? Some of the stems look a little loose… We already told you that you have to tie them a certain way or else the whole thing will fall apart…”

“It’ll be fine! Look—wah!”

As Tribbie predicts, the flower crown unravels barely a minute after it’s been placed on Phainon’s head. Some land on the grass, others slowly drift down onto his lap, creating an unintentionally picturesque scene. Still, showering Phainon in petals had not been their end goal, and Trianne looks dismayed at the sight of the flowers strewn all over the place.

“Ahh! We told you, Trianne!” Tribbie cries. “Come on, let’s pick them up! We’ll show you how to do it again, so make sure you pay attention this time!”

“Okay, okay…!” Pouting a little, Trianne reaches for one of the flowers on Phainon’s lap, but as she does, she pauses. “...Huh?”

Sensing her hesitation, Tribbie looks up from her own task. “Trianne? What’s wrong?”

“Just now… Snowy’s eyes moved.”

Startled, not entirely believing what he just heard, Mydei immediately pushes himself from the tree trunk and stands up straight. “...What? Are you certain?”

Not answering at first, Trianne plucks a bright yellow flower off of Phainon’s lap, raising it above her head, then allowing it to drift back down. Sure enough, Phainon’s eyes flicker, and though he doesn’t seem to be able to follow the flower all the way, he’s clearly staring at it, rather than looking blankly ahead as he usually does.

“His eyes really did move!” Trianne exclaims. “Does that mean he can see now?!”

“We should tell Naxy,” Trinnon pipes up.

“I’ll contact him right away,” Mydei says, already pulling out his teleslate.

For the first time in what feels like an eternity, he feels the beginnings of hope sprouting in his heart.

News spreads throughout the Chrysos Heirs fast, but in spite of the excitement over Phainon’s improvement, Anaxa is insistent that Phainon is allowed the opportunity to get an adequate amount of rest following his last treatment, announcing that they will reconvene in three days time. Those days pass by slowly for Mydei, who remains by Phainon’s side but is unable to curb his restless energy. Phainon is, without a doubt, beginning to be able to track some movement now, and the knowledge that Anaxa possibly has a plan in mind to expedite his recovery makes the wait even more agonizing.

Finally, the day comes, and a small group gathers at the Grove once again, most of them familiar faces. Castorice had accompanied Mydei and Phainon today, and the three meet Hyacine and Anaxa in front of the sage’s lab. Sunday is also there, this time accompanied by Stelle and a short pink-haired girl he doesn’t recognize. Upon seeing Stelle, Castorice seems to light up.

“Oh…! Stelle…”

She fidgets a little, clearly wanting to ask for something, but apparently not having the courage to do so. Thankfully, Stelle seems to know what she wants and opens her arms with a goofy grin on her face.

“C’mere.”

Smiling, Castorice eagerly obliges, running into Stelle’s arms and hugging her tightly. Then, not wanting to leave anyone else out, she hugs Hyacine, who receives her embrace happily, then Little Ica, who lets out a cheerful trill, and finally Anaxa, who doesn’t really reciprocate as strongly but pats her on the back nonetheless. She pauses as she turns to Sunday, but he smiles softly and opens his arms slightly, allowing her to hug him as well. Mydei raises his eyebrows, surprised that a shy girl like Castorice would be so willing to embrace someone that she barely knows, but he’s also aware that she’s been spending more time at the Grove lately, so maybe she and Sunday have had the chance to speak during the times he had been collaborating with Anaxa.

“Awww!” The other pink-haired girl coos when she witnesses the sight. “Do I get one too?”

Castorice lets go of Sunday and turns to the unfamiliar girl, looking unsure of whether a stranger would appreciate her embrace. “Are you alright with it…?”

“Of course! How could I say no to a pretty girl?”

Castorice blushes at the compliment, but seems to be reassured by the smaller girl’s sweet smile and hugs her as well.

“I’m sorry… I don’t believe I know your name,” Castorice admits as she pulls away.

“Oh? Has Stelle been keeping me a secret from everyone? Even though she’s told me about all of you.” She glances coyly at Stelle, who looks away with a grimace, before turning back to Castorice. “Oh well. My name is Cyrene. It’s nice to meet you!”

The name sparks some recognition in Mydei. Phainon had mentioned that name before—it had been during the aftermath of their hot bath competition. Cyrene had been one of the people murdered by the Flame Reaver during the Aedes Elysiae disaster—putting aside the fact that the Flame Reaver had also been a version of Phainon. He doesn’t want to think too much about that fact right now, and instead focuses on the most important thing:

“You’ve known Phainon since before he came to Okhema.”

“Mmhm. Since he was a little boy, in fact. Even though his body is so big now, it doesn’t seem like he’s changed much.” She smiles warmly, turning to where Phainon stands quietly. “I mean, just look at him… At some point, he started trying to act all tough and grown up, but no matter how tall he gets, he still ends up getting fussed over by everyone around him.”

Mydei follows her gaze. While the others were carrying out their greetings and introductions, Anaxa and Hyacine had moved to Phainon’s side, assessing his current condition. Cyrene is right, he muses. Phainon does have the uncanny ability to endear himself to other people, whether it’s intentional on his end or not.

If only he could see how much he’s loved right now.

He’s shaken out of his thoughts when Anaxa and Hyacine approach the group again.

“Hyacine and I have confirmed that Phainon now has the limited ability to track movements. This means that he’s responding well to his current treatments,” Anaxa says. “Now that we know that what we’re doing is working, we can move onto the next phase.” He glances at Sunday. “Are you ready?”

Sunday nods. “I am prepared to begin at any time.”

“Good. Follow me.”

Anaxa heads into his lab, beckoning for Sunday to follow, though Hyacine lingers with the rest of the group. Mydei hasn’t seen her since the black tide incident, and though she looks like her usual self, he decides to ask anyway. “Are you alright?”

Hyacine looks up at him with a gentle smile, immediately knowing what he’s inquiring about. “Professor Anaxa asked me the same thing after we got back from our trip. But I’m fine. The one we should be concerned about is Lord Phainon.”

“Yes, but we should not disregard our own pain. That is what you told me before.”

“Hehe… You’re very considerate, Lord Mydei. I never expected you to use my words against me.” Her expression warms. “But I promise, I’m fine. I wouldn’t be much of a healer if I let a little setback like that get me down. The three of us have gone on several more outings since then, and they all went well. And now that Professor Anaxa has made some progress, I can focus on actually treating Lord Phainon.”

“I see. But if you three plan another excursion in the future, I’ll come. I’m not needed as much around the holy city anymore, so I have significantly more free time than I did before.”

“Oh, that’s great! I’m sure Lord Phainon will be especially pleased to see you with us,” Hyacine says happily.

“Hyacine,” Anaxa calls from within the lab. “Everything is set. Can you bring Phainon in?”

“Coming! I’ll see you in a bit, Lord Mydei.” Hyacine nods at Mydei, then to Stelle and Cyrene. As she takes Phainon’s hand and leads him into the lab, Cyrene hums.

“Hyacine is really cute,” she remarks. “A get-together with me, her, and March would be quite something, don’t you think?”

“Are you talking to me?” Stelle asks, crossing her arms. “Why am I not invited?”

“Feeling left out? You could join us, but you seem like you’d enjoy roughhousing with Phainon more,” Cyrene replies with a giggle. “If it’s just the three of us, I’m the one who’d get excluded!”

Mydei looks at Stelle, outwardly acknowledging her presence for the first time. “You’re here as well.”

“I mean, it’s Phainon, so…” Stelle says. “Also, Dan Heng’s busy today, and someone had to make sure Sunday didn’t get lost on the way to the Grove. And Cyrene wanted me to show her around Okhema now that it’s been mostly repaired, so I’ll be roleplaying as a tour guide later.” She scratches the back of her head. “But Phainon’s the one who knows the most about Okhema’s best sight-seeing spots, doesn’t he? He gave me and Dan Heng some tips when we first landed here… I’ve also read some of the stuff he’s written on the World Wound Web, and it was all pretty in-depth. He must’ve put his whole heart into those blurbs.” A beat. “Actually, the more I think about it, the more I feel like he’s the best person for the job…”

Cyrene giggles again. “Then we’ll just have to make sure Phainon gets better soon, so he can show you how it’s done.”

“Yep. There are some people you really can’t replace…”

Mydei and Castorice lower their heads, finding themselves in silent agreement with Stelle’s statement.

Some time later, Anaxa emerges from the lab looking no worse for wear. “We’re done.”

“How was it?” Mydei asks.

“The treatment itself proceeded without a hitch, but as for whether it’ll actually work, we’ll have to see. It’s likely that the results will be slow to show, as they were for the first phase of treatment.” Anaxa glances back into the lab, and Mydei follows his gaze to where Phainon is seated on a comfortable chair, Hyacine holding his hand and Sunday standing beside him. Stelle peeks in too, raising her eyebrows.

“Huh. Sunday looks totally fine. How’d you do that? The last time I saw someone using mind powers on a Lord Ravager’s victim, they got really messed up.”

“Sunday explained his powers as a tuner in great detail. Naturally, I developed safeguards that were in place throughout the entire treatment. They were sufficient to protect his soul from possible rebounds,” Anaxa replies matter-of-factly.  “Now, if you’re planning on bringing Phainon back to Okhema today, I advise you to wait for at least one hour. It would be better for him to avoid excess stimulation so soon after treatment.”

“I’ll stay with him,” Mydei immediately volunteers, then looks at the others. “The rest of you can return to Okhema, if you wish. We’ll catch up later.”

“No, no, we’ll wait too. Right?” Cyrene says, glancing around, and the others nod in agreement. Then, she turns to Stelle with a wink. “We wouldn’t want Phainon to miss Stelle’s debut as a tour guide, after all!”

Stelle huffs. “With how much you’re hyping me up, I’m gonna have to start charging for tickets.”

In spite of all the jokes, Mydei is silently grateful that Phainon will have so many people waiting for him when he truly awakens.

The next few sessions, which are carried out over intervals of three days, proceed in a similar fashion. Mydei is always there to accompany Phainon, leading him to Anaxa’s lab before the treatments begin and staying with him after they’re over. Today is the same, and as Mydei wiles away the time waiting for Phainon to finish resting, Anaxa approaches him.

“Mydei. A word, if you will.”

Mydei looks up from the bench he and Phainon had been sitting on. “What is it?”

“Where has Phainon been staying since Amphoreus’ restoration began?”

“Aglaea set aside private quarters for him in Marmoreal Palace so that she and Tribios could attend to his needs at any time.”

“I see. I thought as much. That’s not a bad arrangement, but today, I suggest bringing him to a more familiar environment. Somewhere like his home, though I’m sure yours would suffice too.”

It’s quite telling when most other people automatically assume that Phainon and Mydei frequent each other’s residences. However, it is true that they exchanged the keys to their respective homes long ago. Mydei had let himself into Phainon’s abode on more than one occasion, and it’s the same for Phainon. That’s why he focuses not so much on how Anaxa knows, but why he’s making the suggestion in the first place.

“Did something happen during his treatment?” he can’t help but ask. He must sound more worried than he intends to, because Anaxa flashes him a brief but reassuring smile.

“Yes, but it was a good thing. Phainon exhibited more awareness today than in previous sessions, and he was actively observing his surroundings. Both Hyacine and I agreed that it would do him some good to recuperate in the comfort of his home—or yours,” Anaxa adds.

“I see…” Mydei allows his shoulders to relax. “Alright. I’ll bring him back to his home today.”

One hour passes, and Mydei manages to hail a passing dromas caravan en route to Okhema. The trip passes by uneventfully, but Mydei keeps an eye on Phainon the entire time. Anaxa had said that he had been observing his surroundings, but while he does seem more alert than usual, not much else has changed about him. He supposes it’s to be expected—like Trianne had said, the treatments are bound to have a fatiguing effect on Phainon’s already damaged mentality, so Mydei convinces himself to stop fretting.

By the time they disembark in Okhema, it’s already the second quint into the Action Hour, and the streets are bustling as usual. Having had years to hone his reclusive tendencies, Mydei leads Phainon through the most quiet stretches of the holy city—a long but necessary detour if he wants to avoid exposing the broken saviour to the cacophony of the crowds. He does make a few stops along the way to pick up some fresh groceries, though. Phainon hasn’t been home in more than a month, and most of the perishables in his pantry would have spoiled by now. It normally wouldn’t matter, for as the demigod of Worldbearing, he would no longer perceive hunger, but good food would bring comfort to anyone, even the divine, especially if they are suffering from an ailment. And of course, there is also a small part of Mydei that hopes that a familiar taste will spur a quicker recovery, what with the progress that Anaxa had mentioned.

Phainon’s house is situated on a quiet street near Marmoreal Palace, and it is quite humble in spite of the prestigious location. He had been keeping flowers before Okhema’s fall, but they have wilted from neglect, the once colourful ceramic pots and window planters now dull and lifeless. It’s yet another reminder of the state that Phainon has been in, but Mydei shakes the thought from his mind. He is not one to sink into despair, and he can’t allow himself to anyways. Not right now, when he should be focusing on helping his beloved heal.

He fishes the spare keys out of his pocket and lets himself into Phainon’s house, leading him to the living area and sitting him down on the sofa. He then sees that a thin layer of dust has covered mostly everything, but in spite of that, there are signs that the house has been lived in, like ghostly afterimages of the life that its occupant once led: his favourite blue goblet on the dining table, a stack of neatly folded clothes that he had yet to pull away, an antique that he had been in the middle of appraising on his desk. Mydei decides that he’ll help reorganize later, perhaps when Phainon is asleep. For now, he gets to work putting the ingredients he had just bought to good use.

From the bag of groceries, Mydei retrieves a sack of flour, sugar, eggs, goat milk, and fresh fruit—perfect for a batch of simple honeycakes. Within 20 minutes, the food is ready, and Mydei brings a plate back to Phainon, who hasn’t moved from his spot.

“Phainon,” he says, sitting beside him and placing the plate on the small table in front of him. “You need to keep your strength up.”

Phainon’s eyes flicker, and he looks down at the honeycakes. The fact that he reacted at all is promising, but he still makes no move to feed himself, so Mydei takes the fork and knife and begins cutting one of the honeycakes into bite-sized pieces. Then, he takes a piece and presses it to Phainon’s lips.

“Eat,” he says gently but firmly. Phainon’s gaze moves back up, staring at Mydei for a few moments, but he accepts the piece, chewing slowly and swallowing without a problem. Hyacine had mentioned that Phainon was able to eat even before he started treatment, so this is nothing to be excited about, but in light of all the recent developments, Mydei can’t help but feel like they’re making progress.

It takes a while for Phainon to finish the honeycakes. Understandably, he eats rather slowly, but Mydei remains patient, feeding him small pieces until the plate is empty. Once he’s done, Mydei puts the plate back down on the table, deciding to rest for a little while. He leans back against the sofa, his palms against the cushions as he stares blankly at the ceiling. Phainon still doesn’t move, and the quiet between them grows.

Silence isn’t uncommon between them. Mydei and Phainon share an understanding that transcends any spoken language, and sometimes, nothing needs to be said. Nevertheless, Phainon is usually the one who fills the silence with his chatter, and though Mydei is more partial to peace and quiet, he finds himself missing the sound of Phainon’s voice.

Just as he had when he held back the black tide alone in Castrum Kremnos.

That endless battle had lasted for weeks and months on end, to the point where he could no longer tell the passing of time, to the point where his life in Okhema had begun to fade into distant memories. He hadn’t been naive enough to truly believe that they would reunite in some idyllic paradise beyond the sea of souls. But a not-insignificant part of him did yearn painfully for that promised next life, having resigned to the fact that the simple happiness that he and Phainon desired would not be possible to attain in this life.

Yet even after reuniting against all odds in this lifetime, that future still feels like it's slipping through his fingers like grains of sand.

Mydei closes his eyes, forcefully dispelling those thoughts for the second time that day.

If Phainon can’t speak, then Mydei will fill the void in his stead. That is the essence of their relationship: equal parts giving and taking, compensating for what the other lacks. Now and always, forever more.

“That cat-eared thief tried stealing a dress from Aglaea the other day, but she was caught in her golden threads,” Mydei begins absentmindedly. “I had thought Aglaea would be more cross, but instead, it seems like she was amused.”

No answer. Mydei continues.

“Now that her curse has been removed, Castorice has started keeping a garden. It seems like her flowers are growing well, thanks to Hyacine’s instruction. She mentioned wanting to ask you for your advice too, once you have recovered.”

Phainon remains silent and still, as if he hadn’t heard Mydei speaking at all. Mydei continues.

“That reminds me… You may not remember, but during one of our outings, Castorice and Hyacine were discussing a restaurant that they had recently been to. It seems like it specializes in desserts. Perhaps you would be interested in going…”

It goes on like this for some time, Mydei mentioning happenings within the Chrysos Heirs, their correspondence with the Astral Express, humorous incidents in the streets and the baths, and the latest gossip spreading around the World Wound Web. He hopes against hope that one of these topics will sound familiar enough, or perhaps outrageous enough, to prompt a reaction, but in the end, Phainon only responds with silence.

Mydei’s voice trails off. Even with those he’s close to, he’s not one for small talk—that’s more of Phainon’s forte—and keeping up such a one-sided conversation is a little draining. Admittedly, he’s also somewhat disappointed that Phainon hadn’t said anything, with how optimistic Anaxa had seemed about his recovery… But perhaps he should have expected this. After all, Anaxa also said that it would take some time for the results of the treatments to show, so maybe Mydei had been anticipating too much after only a handful of sessions.

He sighs softly, standing up and taking the plate as he does. “I’m going to go clean up. I’ll be right back.”

Resigned, he crosses the living area in a few quick strides, not expecting anything else. But just as he’s about to leave the room, he finally hears it—a familiar voice.

“...My…dei…”

Mydei nearly drops the plate.

His name had been spoken so softly that he fears that he imagined it. Almost afraid of that fear being realized, Mydei turns slowly, staring at Phainon in disbelief.

“...Phainon?”

Phainon doesn’t say anything at first. He’s not even looking at him, his head lowered, his dull, blue eyes unfocused. But sure enough, his lips move again, his voice hoarse from weeks of disuse and barely audible—but undoubtedly there.

“...Mydei…”

The dishes can wait. Mydei immediately moves back to Phainon’s side, placing the plate back on the table so he can touch his arm.

“Phainon,” Mydei breathes. “Can you hear me?”

Phainon doesn’t raise his head, but he seems to react to the sound of Mydei’s voice, the faintest spark of recognition brightening his eyes ever so slightly.

“...Mydei,” he says again, and Mydei nods, squeezing Phainon’s arm reassuringly.

“Yes… Yes, it’s me.” He resists the urge to laugh through his words, the relief nearly overwhelming him. “I’m right here, Phainon. I’m by your side.”

Jolted out of his despondence, his mind is now racing with thoughts. What should he say? What should he do? He had never expected to be the one to bear witness to such a monumental stage in Phainon’s recovery. In the back of his mind, he knows that he should immediately contact the other Chrysos Heirs, but there’s also a part of him that wants a few more moments of privacy with Phainon. There are so many things Mydei wants to say to him right now, so many things that must be said—so many that Mydei can’t single out what he should say first.

But to his surprise, it’s Phainon who continues speaking—

“...I’m…sorry…”

—whispering only those two words. And it’s enough to diminish the borderline celebratory mood that Mydei had been in.

“...I’m sorry… I’m sorry… I’m sorry…”

The apologies slip from Phainon’s lips, not because he is entirely cognizant, but because buried under the rage and hatred that had burned within him for eons, Mydei knows that there must have been a guilty conscience that haunted and tortured him for just as long. Perhaps the the words are murmured in reflex, spurred by the countless emotional scars that he had inflicted upon his own soul with every wound he carved into the bodies of his loved ones. To whom does he apologize? To Mydei himself? To the past Mydeis he killed with his own hands?

Or perhaps to the millions of his own past lives that he had assimilated into himself, burying every Phainon that came before, being buried by every Phainon that came after?

By all rights, Mydei should be horrified and betrayed that Phainon had been able to carry out such deeds so easily, so many times. Even in this cycle, the Flame Reaver—the 33,550,335th Phainon, carrying the burdens of the 33,550,334 who came before him—hadn’t hesitated to drive his sword into Mydei’s vertebrae, hadn’t even stopped to mourn for his beloved as he lay dying in a pool of his own blood.

But when he gazes upon Phainon and sees what it has reduced him to, that righteous anger dissipates like vapour before it can even form. All he can do is stare—

“I’m sorry… I’m sorry… I’m sorry…"

—trying not to come apart at the notion that the first words Phainon had spoken after losing nearly everything about himself—after recovering enough to finally, finally regain something for himself—were for an apology.

“Mydei… I’m…sorry—”

He’s heard enough.

Mydei pulls Phainon close to him, enveloping him in a tight embrace. With his face buried against Mydei’s shoulder, Phainon’s apologies finally cease. He feels slack in Mydei's arms, but the former crown prince can feel that he’s still awake, still at least somewhat aware, and that’s all that matters to him right now.

“...Then, on behalf of every Mydeimos that came before me,” he mutters into his ear, practically kissing it, “I forgive you.”

Would he have forgiven Phainon so easily had the situation been different? Had Phainon come out of his eternal trials more whole? Mydei doesn’t know. But he’s not one to dwell on the what-ifs, either.

All he cares about is ensuring that his beloved—the Phainon that's before him right now, the one and only man whom Mydei had sworn his life to— never gets hurt again.

“And for all the other Phainons that you erased…”

His hold on Phainon tightens.

“...I forgive you as well.”

Phainon’s fingers twitch.

Chapter End Notes

See? Don't worry! Be happy!

Chapter Notes

I've noticed that every time I write a multi-chap fic, there will always be a Chapter. That Chapter will both be very hard for me to write and it will also make me question myself endlessly. Anyway, that's what this chapter was for me, which is why it took a little longer, and I'm still not sure if I like it... But I hope it's ok for readers at least?

I was hoping to finish this fic before 3.5 came out but I don't think that's happening 😭 However, if the next chapter isn't the last one, the one after that definitely will be. Hopefully 3.5 doesn't get me too badly!

Phainon doesn’t speak again for the next few days.

Whether it’s because his momentary capacity for speech was a fluke or some other reason, Mydei doesn’t know. Even so, he doesn’t try to force him to try to talk. Phainon remains noticeably fatigued, tiring at the slightest exertion, despite the fact that he had previously wiped out an entire hoard of black tide creations without effort, and Mydei can only assume that it has to do with the damage done to his mind. Pure instinct does not require thought, but most other things in life do, so he doesn’t rush him.

It’s only when a week passes with no changes does Mydei think to consult Anaxa for his opinion on Phainon’s progress. The scholar spends a few moments considering the possibilities before answering.

“The fact that he was able to say anything at all is quite promising. Unfortunately, it’s too soon to conclude whether it was a happy accident or whether he’s actually making progress in his recovery, especially given that he hasn’t spoken again for almost an entire week.” Anaxa taps his chin in thought. “He said your name, yes? I surmise that he was able to recognize you were in the room with him and reacted accordingly. Of course, there’s also a possibility that he was simply calling for you out of habit.”

“Habit?” Mydei repeats.

“I don’t think anyone can understate how much Phainon talked about you,” Anaxa continues. “Among all the Chrysos Heirs, you’re probably the one who has made the strongest impression on him. It only follows, then, that memories of you would resurface before everything else.”

Mydei looks down, torn. He doesn’t like the thought of his and Phainon’s “conversation” having been a product of Phainon’s memories, rather than a sign of improvement in his cognition, but he’s admittedly partial to the idea of being that important to him.

“Incidentally…” Anaxa’s voice shakes him out of his reverie. “What else did Phainon say to you?”

The former crown prince pauses, remembering the tortured apologies that had been whispered to him in the room that day, and looks away.

“...Just my name. Nothing else,” he finally says.

Anaxa watches him quietly, and Mydei has the feeling that he doesn’t entirely believe him. But thankfully, the scholar seems to recognize the reasons behind Mydei’s lie and doesn’t press him for more details.

Phainon does begin showing marked signs of improvement as more time passes. His treatments seem to be working well, and with Mydei escorting him back home after his sessions, he’s able to take note of the changes. Phainon remains alert for longer periods of time, visibly reacting to what happens around him. On more than one occasion, Mydei has observed him watching dromases at rest and chimeras at play, and though he appears tired, his half-lidded eyes keenly follow the path of any of the butterfly-like nymphs that happen to flutter past his head. One day, when he sees Phainon staring at a batch of yellow flowers on display in a flower shop, he comes up with an idea, touching his arm gently to get his attention. Phainon turns his head, now looking at Mydei, as if waiting for him to say something.

He thinks back to what Hyacine had told him once, before they were about to depart the Grove after a session. “Lord Phainon is getting better, so you might be able to communicate with him now. If you talk to him, make sure your sentences are short and easy to understand. If you want to ask him something, try to keep it to things he can respond to with gestures or one-word answers,” she had said. They’re simple enough instructions to follow, but Mydei hadn’t found an opportunity to try it until now.

He points at the yellow flowers, making sure Phainon’s eyes can trace his index finger to the display. “Do you like those? Nod if yes.”

To his delight, Phainon nods.

“Do you want them?”

He nods again, and Mydei feels himself smiling. Though Phainon hadn’t been able to respond verbally, he was listening, and he had understood what he had asked him. It’s a start.

He purchases a few stems of the flowers, slipping them into one of Phainon’s hands. Then, he takes his free hand, leading him back to his home. Phainon lets go of neither the flowers nor Mydei the entire way back.

Finally, one week later, Phainon manages to speak again.

It’s such a mundane thing, but in these extraordinary circumstances, the chance to return to mundanity is one of the most welcome gifts of them all.

That’s why, when Mydei asks if Phainon wants to go on a walk together, and Phainon responds with a quiet “Yes,” Mydei is quick to spread the news to the others—but not before holding his beloved tightly.

The improvements only continue from there, and within another week, Phainon is beginning to answer Mydei more regularly, though his speech is often slow and punctuated by pauses, and only ever spoken in response to simple questions. He struggles with more complex sentences and never initiates conversations, but Hyacine informs Mydei that this is to be expected from someone with his level of brain damage, and that his progress is something to celebrate nevertheless.

Eager to discuss the changes, Anaxa wastes no time in gathering the Chrysos Heirs for another meeting a few days after the good news. This time, the group consists of himself, Hyacine, Castorice, Aglaea, and, of course, Mydei.

“So, we have now confirmed, without a shadow of doubt, that Phainon is reacting to visual and auditory stimuli and understands simple questions. He also is capable of speech, but only in brief sentences.” Anaxa glances at Mydei. “Do I have that right?”

The Kremnoan nods. “That’s correct.”

“Then his recovery is proceeding smoothly, and at a much faster pace than I had initially hypothesized,” Anaxa announces to the other Chrysos Heirs. “But before we move onto phase three—the phase concerning any possible memory loss—we should first determine what Phainon actually remembers.”

“How do you suggest we do that?” Aglaea asks.

“We can gauge where he is by how well he recognizes us. It’s not the most reliable test, but it will be simple enough to perform, and it won’t exert him too much.” Anaxa’s one working eye drifts to a quiet corner in the room, where Phainon is currently seated on a comfortable armchair, holding Little Ica in his arms. “Just keep his mental state in mind, and don’t be too disappointed if he doesn’t remember who you are.”

Aglaea raises her eyebrows. “I believe everyone in this room was already prepared for that possibility, even without you highlighting it. Are you simply trying to reassure yourself, Anaxagoras?”

“What an absurd proposition. Why would I need to reassure myself?” Anaxa sniffs. “Now, if you’re all ready, let’s go speak to him. Try not to overwhelm him.”

Without waiting for the others to follow, Anaxa approaches Phainon first, calling out to him more gently. “Phainon.”

At the sound of Anaxa’s voice, Phainon raises his head and turns towards him, but he doesn’t say anything. Encouraged by the reaction nonetheless, Anaxa continues.

“Do you know who I am?”

Phainon spends some time staring at his former teacher blankly, and for a moment, it doesn’t seem like he’ll answer. But then, his lips move, allowing his barely audible voice to be heard.

“...Professor…Anaxa.”

“...Ha. Not entirely correct, but I’ll let it slide this time on the account of your condition.” Despite what he says, Anaxa’s words lack any bite—in fact, he seems more relieved than anything else. He steps aside for the other Chrysos Heirs, who are close behind him. “Can you tell me the names of everyone else gathered here?”

Phainon raises his head further, his half-lidded eyes slowly moving from one person to the other.

“...Miss Castorice. Hyacine. Aglaea…” His gaze falls on Mydei, and the former crown prince swears that he sees his eyes soften. “...Mydei.”

Trying to suppress their glee, Castorice and Hyacine throw their arms around one another and hug each other tightly, bright smiles on their faces. Reacting to Hyacine’s joy, Little Ica trills happily in Phainon’s arms. Aglaea is also smiling, having let out the breath she was holding. Satisfied with the results, Anaxa turns back to Phainon again.

“Now… Tell me your own name.”

Phainon pauses, as if having to deliberate on the answer. Then, he speaks slowly.

“Khaslana…of Aedes Elysiae,” he mumbles. His tone is dull, unenergetic, and expectedly, his speech is riddled by long pauses as he struggles to maintain a firm grasp on his words. “Phainon…warrior of…Okhema.”

Behind Anaxa, Hyacine and Castorice smile at each other again. Even Aglaea looks more pleased than usual—at least, until Phainon says what he does next:

“Lord Ravager…Irontomb.”

The hopeful mood diminishes immediately. Smiles fade, and Anaxa’s brow furrows. Startled by such an out-of-pocket answer, Mydei lips part to speak, his heart sinking, but as usual, it’s Aglaea who steps forward first, her voice stern and sharp.

“Anaxagoras, what is the meaning of this? Why is he introducing himself as the Lord Ravager?”

“Patience, woman. I’m trying to figure that out myself.” Anaxa turns back to Phainon, addressing him once more. “Tell me your name again.”

“...Khaslana. Phainon…” There’s another brief pause before he continues. “...Irontomb.”

Staring at Phainon for a little longer, Anaxa sighs, taking a step back. “...Well. We did manage to confirm that he does remember who we are, and that he maintains a sense of identity. In light of what he had done to himself millions of times, that’s a good sign…”

Mydei looks down, remembering the repeated apologies that Phainon had whispered in his torment not too long ago, but he doesn’t say anything. Anaxa has also fallen silent, considering his options before turning to face the others. “I’m going to contact the Astral Express. They’ll have more information on the Lord Ravagers than we do. Let’s adjourn this meeting for now.”

The gathered Chrysos Heirs are left to wait things out as Anaxa excuses himself to sort out this unexpected development. The silence feels heavier than usual, but Mydei doesn’t need to be a mind reader to guess why. In no mood to converse with such a bitter taste left in his mouth, he simply stands beside the seated Phainon as usual, while Castorice kneels by the swordsman’s other side to hold his hand. Luckily, Phainon doesn’t seem to be completely aware of the effect he’s had on the others, and with no one else actively addressing him, he has gone still and quiet, his mind having drifted off once again.

After what feels like an eternity, Anaxa returns to the room, a grim look on his face.

“I was able to reach Dan Heng,” he says, already answering everyone’s questions before they can even form. “He told me that during the restoration process, they were unable to completely decouple Phainon from Irontomb. That is to say, his soul—or rather, his ‘code,’ as they called it—was so intertwined with the entity that doing so carried a very high risk of corrupting his existence and rendering him unable to be restored at all.”

It’s not something that Mydei wants to hear—the thought of Phainon being unable to exist without the thing that had caused all of them so much pain, that had caused him so much pain, that had used him and forced him to fight and endure beyond his limits until he was reduced to an empty shell, is difficult to stomach. Beside Phainon, Castorice looks up, looking equally upset. “What does that mean for Lord Phainon, then?” she asks, unable to conceal the apprehension in her voice.

“Nothing, from the sounds of it. It doesn’t seem like there have been any negative side effects so far, even after he encountered the black tide. If anything, Phainon now carries Irontomb’s power within him, and the entirety of it is at his disposal to use. Ideally, he would never be placed in any situation where he would have to resort to doing so.” The sage sighs. “If he truly can’t exist without Irontomb at this point in time, then there’s nothing to be done about it. At any rate, I was assured that it’s completely inert, and it’s no longer a threat to anyone’s safety, nor is it likely to interfere with Phainon's recovery, so we won’t have to worry about that.”

There’s a pregnant pause in the room before Anaxa continues, voicing the thought that no one else dares to. “Of course,” he says. “That is before we consider how it may affect his self-perception once he does begin regaining more awareness.”

Finding that notion unpleasant to dwell on, Mydei’s hand automatically moves to Phainon’s shoulder, squeezing it tightly. The swordsman looks up at him inquisitively, but doesn’t say anything.

In the end, Anaxa and Hyacine conclude that it would be best to proceed with Phainon’s treatment as planned. And slowly but surely, as the days pass, Phainon’s condition continues to improve. Mydei puts aside thoughts of the Lord Ravager within his beloved, instead focusing his energy into doing what he can to help him heal. With Okhema now fully restored, the Kremnoan has an abundance of free time, and he uses that time to continue escorting Phainon to and from the Grove, participating in Hyacine’s and Castorice’s planned excursions, and otherwise accompanying Phainon as he slowly recovers. Mydei has never considered himself much of a caretaker, but being able to provide these simple things for the swordsman does bring him comfort, and he can only hope that Phainon feels the same.

The day of another scheduled session comes. Mydei approaches Phainon, who’s sitting quietly at the edge of his bed, and touches the back of his hand.

“Phainon. Let’s go.”

Mydei ensures Phainon raises his head and makes eye contact with him before he takes his hand and pulls him to his feet. Then, as always, he leads him out of the house before locking the door behind him and begins the journey to the Grove.

He fully expects to pass the journey in silence—Mydei has, regrettably, gotten used to the quiet that had replaced Phainon’s constant chatter. But to his surprise, Phainon actually speaks today.

“Where…?”

The fact that he had asked at all isn’t that startling; Phainon had already begun initiating conversations without prompting at home. But this is the first time he has spoken during an outing.

“We’re going to the Grove. You have another scheduled treatment today,” Mydei answers, then pauses, wondering if that was too hard to understand. He adds, “We’re seeing Anaxagoras and Hyacine.”

Phainon doesn’t answer for a while, simply walking quietly behind Mydei. Then, he stops, and feeling the sudden resistance, Mydei stops too, turning around and staring at Phainon questioningly.

“...Phainon?” he asks. “What’s wrong? Do you not want to go?”

Phainon looks down, his eyebrows furrowing, and Mydei can tell that he’s trying to convey what he wants to say. The former crown prince remains patient, knowing that such things can’t be rushed—they’re still early, anyway, so they have time. After a while, Phainon seems to figure out how to string his words together, then starts speaking again.

“...Professor Anaxa…and Hyacine,” he mumbles. “Lately… They’re tired.”

Mydei blinks. He supposes that much is to be expected. Hyacine has been juggling Phainon’s treatments, her duties at the rebuilt Twilight Courtyard, her usual therapeutic services, and the various outings she has planned with Castorice, while Anaxa has been burning the midnight oil to juggle his research and ensure his alchemy has the intended restorative effect on Phainon’s damaged soul. Both of them are known for their ability to disguise their fatigue, so for Phainon to take note of such subtleties is a sign that he’s on the mend.

But why would he bring that up now?

Mydei doesn’t need to ponder that for long.

“It’s…because of me. It’s my…fault.”

The quiet remark has Mydei staring in stunned silence at Phainon as he continues.

“I’m…hurting them. Again and again.”

Again, Phainon is thinking of others more than himself, again, Phainon is blaming himself for things outside of his control. Mydei finally finds his voice amidst the budding ache in his chest. “...It would hurt them more to hear you say that,” he says with surety, and he knows it to be fact. But it doesn’t seem to convince Phainon, who looks torn.

“Why…?”

“Because you’re important to them. Because they care about you.”

“But I’m…the Flame Reaver. And I’m…Irontomb.”

Mydei goes silent, the possibility he had been hoping to deny—the possibility of Phainon remembering who he was, yet forgetting who he was, losing himself to all of his overlapping identities—rearing its ugly head.

“I’m…different now. After everything I’ve done… Can I still…stay here? With everyone?”

Stop it.

“Shouldn’t I…leave?”

No.

“I’m…” Phainon’s eyes quiver. “I’m hurting you too…Mydei. Like always —”

Feeling himself coming undone at that, Mydei abruptly grabs Phainon by upper arms, his grip tightening hard enough to bruise, the suddenness of the gesture shaking the hapless swordsman’s body. Phainon barely reacts to the pain or the jostling, perhaps because he doesn't yet have the mental capacity to perceive them, or perhaps because the sensation is so minute compared to the millions of coreflames that had burned him alive for far too many eternities. Either way, Mydei’s grasp doesn’t loosen, for his emotions are currently what direct him.

“You will always… always be one of us,” he whispers, his tone harsh with anguish at the thought that Phainon would even think of himself as anything less than a person when he bears a heart that is so painfully human— that he would even think of isolating himself, of willfully disappearing from Mydei’s life when he had already been so close to losing him.

That’s why he knows it needs to be said:

“No matter what you’ve turned yourself into, or what you’ve been forced to transform into… It doesn’t change anything.”

That’s why he resolves to leave nothing important unsaid ever again.

“You will always be our Phainon. Always.”

He doesn’t know whether his words actually get through. Phainon simply stares at Mydei, a vacant look in his eyes. Then, his expression slackens, and he looks down blankly. And when Mydei finally releases his arms and slowly takes his hand to lead him again, much gentler than before, Phainon no longer protests.

They pass the rest of the journey through Okhema in silence, and even when they board the dromas caravan waiting for them, neither of them say a word. Mydei still feels somewhat unsettled, but he’s significantly calmer now, and the silence allows him to repeatedly turning over his and Phainon’s conversation in his mind. It's made him recognize, belatedly, that all of them are essentially treating the former Deliverer without his consent, and though he can’t imagine that Phainon would have wanted to remain in his vegetative state forever, unable to see, hear, or talk to anyone he loved again, it does bring other thoughts to mind—thoughts about what to do with their new future.

If he had known that the Flame-Chase Journey was a lie—if he had known the Trailblazer would arrive and free them all from Lygus’ shackles—what would he have chosen to do with his newfound freedom?

It’s not something that even Mydei has considered for himself outside of hypothetical conversations with Phainon. Even in those discussions, he had rarely indulged the former Deliverer, hardly able to conceive of a future beyond his duties as Castrum Kremnos’ heir apparent, and later, the demigod of Strife. Not in this lifetime, anyway.

But Phainon was a different story, eager to chatter on about the possibilities —and now that Mydei thinks about it, he realizes that the swordsman had been trying to give him some ideas of his own. “If I wasn’t the Deliverer, maybe I’d be a wanderer, or a mercenary, traveling all over Amphoreus and seeing all there is to see,” he had said in one of their conversations on the topic, his eyes sparkling with child-like wonder as he envisioned such a life. “Professor Anaxa praises my debate skills as well, so maybe I could even be a scholar. What do you think, Mydei? Can you imagine me as one of the Grove’s intellectuals?”

He had turned and grinned at Mydei then, and his cheeky expression had filled Mydei with the urge to knock him down a few pegs. After that, their conversation devolved into their usual nonsensical bickering, and then a competition that had ultimately led to them both being scolded by Aglaea. In spite of that, Phainon had remained his usual cheerful and energetic self for the rest of the day, eventually inviting (dragging) Mydei to the baths as if nothing had happened.

When Mydei’s eyes drift to Phainon now, sitting beside him in quiet despondence, his heart aches for what had once been, and what could have been had Phainon not sacrificed himself millions of times over—all for the faint hope that everyone else could finally live to see the dawn.

Mydei finds himself wondering whether Phainon had ever considered a place for himself in the future he suffered for.

No, he knows the answer to that already.

Rather, the better question is probably this: When Phainon had stopped seeing himself as part of the world he was trying so hard to save?

Mydei is already speaking before he realizes. “Phainon,” he says softly, watching him out of the corner of his eye. He waits until he sees Phainon raising his head and turning to him before continuing. “What is your wish?”

“Wish…” Phainon is quiet at first, but he answers relatively easily. “To fulfill…everyone’s wishes. And if I can't...” His gaze lowers. “Pass them on…to tomorrow.”

Mydei feels his fists clenching, his gauntlets digging into his palm. Had they met his bare skin, he’s certain they would have drawn blood.

Of course Phainon would say something like that. Of course that would be his first answer. Even after burning himself to ashes a million times over for the world, he still would not consider his own wants, but what truly hurts is how automatic the reply had been, as if there was no other possibility but for him to act as the receptacle of the wishes of other people. “I’m not talking about the Deliverer’s wishes,” he says a little more harshly than he intends to. “I’m talking about yours. What does Phainon want? What does Khaslana want?”

The white-haired man falls silent, a look of confusion spreading across his face. Cognizant of his own agitation, Mydei takes a deep breath to calm himself down before trying again. Then, he turns to face Phainon fully, reaching over to frame his face with both of his hands.

“If you truly wish to fulfill everyone else’s wishes,” Mydei speaks more gently this time, thumbing a stray lock of white hair away from Phainon’s cheek. “Then allow me to share what mine is.”

He leans forward until their foreheads are touching. Phainon doesn’t reciprocate as he usually does, but Mydei can tell that he’s still aware, still watching him, still listening. That’s all he needs.

“My wish…is to hear you speak of your own wants. To listen to what you desire from the bottom of your heart,” Mydei says. “So for the sake of that wish…will you tell me, Phainon?”

Phainon’s eyes flicker, the change barely perceptible if not for the fact that their faces are so close, and Mydei knows he understood. Even so, he doesn’t say anything for the longest time. Mydei fears he simply won’t. Getting him to voice his true thoughts had been like pulling teeth even when he was mentally sound, let alone now, while he’s so impaired. But Mydei holds onto the hope that he’s gotten through to Phainon, and that hope is rewarded when his lips finally move in the faintest of whispers.

“I want…”

His voice trembles ever so slightly.

“...I want…to go home…”

He mouths his desire, as if even voicing into existence is the greatest of sins —even though the wish is so innocent in its simplicity, and a sentiment that Mydei has echoed many times throughout much of his own shattered childhood and his adult life.

“...You want to go back to Aedes Elysiae,” Mydei says.

“Aedes Elysiae…” Phainon looks down—as far down as he can while Mydei still holds his face. “...I can’t…remember.”

Mydei’s eyes widen slightly, staring at the swordsman in mild disbelief. “...Do you mean to say that you can’t remember your homeland?”

Phainon falls silent, and the Kremnoan can’t tell whether it’s in confirmation or denial. Anything is possible with the mental damage he has suffered, but the thought that it has erased even the burning hatred that had arisen from an even more powerful love is almost inconceivable. Mydei doesn’t want to believe that Phainon has lost even that part of himself, that core aspect of his being that had motivated him for so long.

“...You loved Aedes Elysiae,” Mydei finally says after some deliberation, his mind drifting to all those times Phainon had come close to speaking of his homeland, yet held his tongue. He wishes he had prodded him more.

Then at least he’d have some description of it for Phainon now. “You never spoke of it…but you loved it.”

“Loved…” Phainon mumbles the word, pausing, as if he needs to turn it over on his tongue. “I loved… Aedes Elysiae,” he repeats. “The golden wheat fields… The vast sea… The people who lived there...”

So he remembers, then. That comes as a relief to Mydei. But strangely enough, Phainon doesn’t seem to be comforted.

“So why…did I set it aflame…? Why did I kill everyone…over and over again…?”

…Of course.

Mydei’s heart sinks when the dreadful realization hits him. The Flame Reaver had appeared in Aedes Elysiae, bringing the black tide with him—in this cycle, and many more before that. And Phainon would have memories of the bloodshed, as well as the conflagration that followed the disaster, all brought about by his own two hands.

You had no choice, he wants to say, but even as he turns the words over on his tongue, they sound insincere, like nothing more than lip service. He doesn’t really know if it’s the truth, besides, because the undeniable reality is that after living through Amphoreus’ cycles millions upon millions of times, Phainon is now capable of killing his friends, family, and allies without hesitation.

As with before, Mydei doesn’t feel any revulsion at the fact, for he knows that no Phainon would have ever made the decision to turn his blade on everything and everyone he loved lightly. He had possessed the willpower to carry through with his convictions, come what may, no matter what he had to do, completely alone and worn as thin as he may have been, and to Mydei, that is true strength.

But it does leave him with no words of comfort for Phainon. Even if the swordsman could understand what he was saying in its entirety, would Mydei even be able to provide him with solace?

In the end, all he can do is hold Phainon tightly. Where words fail him, action will not.

You won’t have to stain your hands with blood again. You won’t have to fight alone again.

He only hopes that their closeness will convey this much.

Phainon doesn’t reciprocate, but he doesn’t pull away either, allowing himself to be cradled in Mydei’s arms until their caravan arrives at the Grove.

The session takes a little longer than usual today. When the door to Anaxa’s lab finally opens, only Hyacine comes out. True to Phainon’s words, she does look a little more tired than usual, but she greets those waiting outside —this time, Mydei, Cyrene, and Dan Heng—with her usual sweet smiles.

“You’re all still here…except for Grayie and your other pink-haired friend. Did they wander off?” she asks Dan Heng, and he nods.

“March wanted to take a walk around the Grove, so Stelle just went with her. Sunday and I were going to reconvene with them after Phainon’s treatment was over, but…it seems like it’s not done yet? Did everything go smoothly?”

Mydei looks up. There’s usually a slight delay before Phainon, Sunday, and Anaxa exit the lab; if Phainon isn't led outside by Anaxa, Mydei is allowed in to guide him out. This time, though, the door remains closed. Hyacine offers them both a helpless smile.

“I think Sunnie would be able to explain it better than me, but it seems like he encountered some difficulties when he used his tuning on Lord Phainon today. He and Professor Anaxa are discussing that right now,” Hyacine replies, then turns to Mydei. “Professor Anaxa asked me to talk to you about that, actually… I couldn’t help but notice you both seemed a bit down when you arrived. Did something happen between you two on the way here?”

“...Not necessarily,” Mydei says after a brief pause. “We had some… conversations.”

“Oh! Lord Phainon was able to hold multiple conversations with you? That’s good!” Hyacine tilts her head. “But they weren't exactly happy, were they?”

“We didn’t get into an argument, if that’s what you were wondering.” The former crown prince runs a hand through his messy golden hair, trying to figure out what to say. He is not particularly well-known for his eloquence, but in this case, he stalls not for a lack of words, but for indecision.

He doesn’t feel as if it’s his place to share what Phainon had whispered to him at his most vulnerable. But if he doesn’t voice Phainon’s wishes, who will?

“Well, Mydei? Would you like to share your thoughts with the rest of us?”

Jolted out of his deliberation, Mydei turns around at the sound of the new voice. Anaxa and Sunday had exited the lab while he was thinking, and Anaxa now scrutinizes him with crossed arms before adding, “The more we know about Phainon’s current state, the better.”

“His current state?” Mydei repeats, alarmed. “Did something happen after all?”

“It is not anything so drastic, Mr. Mydeimos,” Sunday replies, keeping his tone even. Hearing him speaking so calmly does provide Mydei with some reassurance. “We were able to complete the treatment as planned. However, Mr. Phainon exhibited some dissonance today. Typically, this arises due to negative emotions, and while it has since been alleviated, Miss Hyacine, Mr. Anaxagoras and I were somewhat puzzled about the cause.”

“...I see.” Mydei sighs. Now, even Cyrene and Dan Heng are staring at him, and he feels as if he’s been left with no choice. “For his sake,” he begins. “Will you swear that this conversation will not be spoken of beyond these walls?”

“Well, I don’t think any of us can guarantee that we won’t share what we hear with the other Chrysos Heirs, seeing as this does concern Phainon,” Anaxa answers. “But if you’re speaking of anyone outside of Aglaea’s inner circle, then I don’t believe there’s any need for concern.”

Fair enough. Maybe having others who know will be beneficial to Phainon too. As much as it pains him, Mydei is aware his own limits, and there will always be things that he is unable to provide, needs he will be unable to attend to—but if the others are aware of those needs, that won’t be an issue. Deeming the answer acceptable, Mydei tells everyone about the conversations he had with Phainon that morning—both before and after they boarded the dromas caravan—though he keeps it brief, leaving out some of the finer details for Phainon’s sake.

After letting the explanation settle in, Anaxa hums thoughtfully. “I see… As more of Phainon’s awareness returns, so, too, do the memories of the atrocities he had committed… It makes sense, although it seems like he doesn’t remember other things quite yet.” The scholar raises his head, eyeing Dan Heng. “You look like you have something you’d like to add, Dan Heng. Speak.”

A little startled that he had been called on, Dan Heng takes a moment to gather his thoughts before speaking. “I’m not sure if it helps at all, but I was just thinking… There’s a condition known as ‘mara’ where I come from. It’s a blight caused by the Aeon of Abundance, bestowing immortality upon those who have it… But the longer one lives, the more the ego erodes. This is because, over the course of an endless life, the mind collapses under the accumulation of memories. And the most vivid memories are, invariably, the ones with the strongest negative emotions associated with them, which is what eventually drives people to madness.”

“How awful…” Hyacine whispers. “Is there a cure for this condition?”

“No, not yet. That’s why I wasn’t sure whether my saying anything would help. And it’s not like Phainon has been afflicted by the Abundance either, so his condition is distinct to begin with,” Dan Heng replies. “It’s just that, when Mydei told us that Phainon could only remember his more sorrowful experiences, I couldn’t help but think about the mara-struck.”

Everyone in the room falls silent, ruminating. But then, a bright voice cuts through the hush.

“Well! Just knowing that they’re not the same means that there’s still hope for Phainon, right?”

They all turn to Cyrene, who had spoken for the first time since the gathering began. With everyone’s attention on her, she continues.

“If Phainon can only remember his saddest memories right now, then we just need to help him remember his happier ones,” she says. “Or better yet, help him make new memories—memories that shine brighter than anything else.”

“While that’s a logical suggestion and simple enough in theory, I’m quite curious about how you intend to put this into practice,” Anaxa remarks. “Where would we even start?”

“Oh, that’s easy.”

Cyrene smiles knowingly, glancing into the lab, where Phainon remains sitting quietly.

“For the warrior who bore the world on his shoulders for so long to finally be able to relieve his burdens in the place where it all began… Wouldn’t that be romantic?”

Understanding dawns on Mydei immediately. "You mean to say... We should bring him back home."

"Mmhm!"

She glances around at everyone in the room. "So? How about we plan a trip to Aedes Elysiae?"
