Chapter Notes

As I mentioned in the previous chapter, I wasn't able to get all of this fic done before 3.5, but a majority of it was already planned before the patch, so there won't be any spoilers for 3.5 in this chapter...or the rest of the chapters, for that matter.

This chapter's gonna be a bit more light-hearted! After the last two I thought it'd be good to have a break from the angst 😂

“So to recount your idea for those who weren’t there,” Anaxa says a few days later, after the Chrysos Heirs, Stelle, and Dan Heng have all gathered in one of Marmoreal Palace’s conference rooms. “You believe that bringing Phainon back to Aedes Elysiae will help him recover. Is there basis behind your theory, Cyrene?” he asks.

“They say that home is where the heart is,” Cyrene replies easily. “And I was thinking, maybe Phainon just needs a little bit of help finding his heart again. What better way to do that than to bring him back to his beloved home?”

“Lord Phainon did love his home a lot,” Castorice concurs. “Even though he came to Okhema young, even though he always tried to smile for everyone… He carried the weight of his loss for so long.”

Hearing Castorice’s agreement, Anaxa turns to Stelle and Dan Heng. “How far along are you in Amphoreus’ restoration process?”

“We’re not directly involved,” Dan Heng says. “The ones who are are focusing more on the larger city-states first. But I don’t think they would be opposed to shifting their focus to Aedes Elysiae.”

“It’s taking quite a while, isn’t it?” Cipher remarks, and though her tone is nonchalant, she observes both Dan Heng and Stelle with sharp eyes. “I’ve

been around the block, and a lot of places are still in ruins, or worse, corrupted, even though it’s been more than two months.”

“Time passes faster within the simulation—within Amphoreus than it does outside of it. For those on the outside, it’s only been a few days," Dan Heng explains. "Given how much damage Irontomb did, it may take a while longer to restore everything.”

Cipher clicks her tongue, her tail twitching irritably. “What a pain…”

“That’s quite the discrepancy indeed,” Anaxa says pensively. “Not that it’s of any consequence to us, seeing as none of us can leave Amphoreus at the moment. Let us turn our attention back to the most pressing matter: how quickly will your comrades be able to restore Aedes Elysiae?”

For the first time, Stelle speaks up. “Probably not as long as a place like Styxia or Janusopolis? Aedes Elysiae is pretty small. I bet it doesn’t even take up that much space on the server. The only assets they’d have to load in are all the wheat stalks, the wheelbarrows, the houses, those windmills, the scarecrows, and maybe that weird boat that’s always floating in the distance. Most of it is out of bounds, anyway. I can’t even interact with the doors of the houses.”

Dan Heng throws an exasperated look her way. “What are you talking about…?”

“...And why do you know about Aedes Elysiae?” Mydei asks, narrowing his eyes at Stelle. She looks away with a grimace and quickly waves her arms in front of her, knowing the folly of trying to get between him and Phainon.

“Don’t look at me like that! It’s really hard to explain. Blame Lygus.”

While that’s easy enough to do, unfortunately for Stelle, Lygus had been rendered non-functional after the final battle, leaving her as the only possible target for Mydei’s ire. He continues staring a hole right through her until she tries to change the subject.

“Anyway, when’s the trip?”

“Obviously, it will have to wait until Aedes Elysiae and the paths leading to it are completely restored.” Anaxa raises his head, looking pointedly at Aglaea. “And of course, we’ll need to secure the esteemed Lady Goldweaver’s approval for Phainon’s extended leave as well.”

Aglaea returns Anaxa’s look with a disdainful glance. “Phainon is free to come and go as he pleases. I have not imposed any restrictions on his movements. And even if I had, I would have no qualms about allowing him beyond the borders of Okhema and the Grove as long as such excursions would be able to help him recover.”

“But it’ll still take some time for Aedes Elysiae to be restored, right?” Tribbie pipes up. “Can we do anything for Snowy while we wait?”

“Just what you’ve been doing already—making sure he’s as comfortable as possible,” Hyacine says. “Now that he’s more aware, he’ll definitely be able to appreciate your efforts!”

“Okay! We’ll sing lots for him, then!”

Cyrene giggles at Tribbie’s enthusiasm. “Even without going back to Aedes Elysiae, it seems like Phainon’s going to be able to make lots of happy memories.” As the conversation continues, she looks up at Mydei, who hasn’t said anything since he had questioned Stelle about Aedes Elysiae, and adds, “Why don’t you do the honours of being part of his first ones?”

Mydei blinks, a little startled at the abrupt remark. “...Me?”

“Yes, you. You’re very special to him, you know,” she says with a wink. “Why don’t you go see him right now? Seeing us talk in such hush-hush tones is probably making him feel lonely.”

“...How about you?” he asks. “Were you not childhood friends with him? I’m sure he’d appreciate your presence as well.”

“That’s sweet of you to invite me, but won’t I just be third-wheeling the whole time?” Laughing at the face Mydei makes, she holds her hands behind her back coyly. “I’m preparing a little special something for him, but I’ll need Stelle’s and March’s help for that, so I’m going to be a bit busy for the next few days. I’m sure he won’t mind—we’ll have plenty of time to catch up afterwards.”

Mydei glances over to where Phainon is currently standing facing away from the group. Though the other Chrysos Heirs are not making an effort to outright exclude him from the conversation, he definitely does look a little pitiful not being part of it at all, and the fact that he hasn’t made an effort to join is another painful reminder that, in spite of all his improvements, he remains far from what he used to be.

Encouraged by the nod that Cyrene gives him, Mydei quietly excuses himself from the meeting and walks over to Phainon. At his approach, the swordsman raises his head and turns around. He’s holding Little Ica again —it’s a habit he seems to have developed since he began receiving treatment—and is absentmindedly stroking their mane, though he stops when Mydei nears, unable to focus on more than one thing at a time in his current state.

“Why don’t we take a walk around Marmoreal Palace?” Mydei begins. Phainon stares at him, then glances past his shoulder. Some of the Chrysos Heirs have dispersed already, but others, like Aglaea and Anaxa, still linger, locked in a deep discussion. He looks back to Mydei questioningly, and the former crown prince understands what he’s trying to ask.

“The meeting is over, and I have the rest of the afternoon off. Shall we take a walk together?” he asks again, just in case Phainon has forgotten— Hyacine had mentioned that things he has just been told or asked might slip from his mind easily, but that’s to be expected with his current affliction. Phainon, at least, seems partial to the idea of a walk, and he nods more eagerly than usual. But before he can do anything else, they hear Hyacine’s voice sound from the hall.

“Little Ica! Where are you?”

“Doot-doot!”

At her call, Little Ica rises from Phainon’s arms and floats towards the hall. Phainon stares after them, but he makes no move to stop them. As Mydei watches, he realizes that the swordsman may have enjoyed petting the tiny pegasus but currently lacks the faculties to ask for more time with them.

“If you want Ica to stay, I’m sure Hyacine would allow it. I’ll ask her, if you’d like.”

Phainon shakes his head, letting his arms fall to his sides. Mydei doesn’t seem that convinced, but then, the swordsman begins speaking.

“Ica…is rounder,” he says slowly.

Quirking his eyebrow at such an out-of-pocket statement, Mydei glances back towards the door as Little Ica disappears behind it. Now that he thinks about it, they are quite rotund. “Yes. I’ve heard that they have quite the appetite.”

“Appetite… That’s good.” The corners of Phainon’s mouth twitch upwards. “Before, in the Vortex of Genesis… They were thinner. They stopped eating… Because Hyacine was gone.”

The Vortex of Genesis?

Mydei stares at Phainon, a little puzzled. Based on what Stelle had shared with all of them, Phainon had been alone with Lygus until she had reached his side. At the end of the world, Mydei himself had sensed Hyacine’s ascent into divinity, and he had seen her shimmering barriers guarding the panicked civilians of Okhema as he raced through the fallen holy city to help intercept the black tide and the Flame Reaver’s assault. While it’s possible that she had sent Little Ica away to keep them safe, Mydei believes it’s more likely that they stayed with her until the very end.

What exactly is he remembering? Mydei makes a note to ask Stelle for clarification later on, and see if she can corroborate what Phainon had said.

“Do you want Ica to stay with you? You have one more chance to change your mind, or else you’ll have to settle for my company alone,” Mydei says.

Phainon shakes his head again, though he remains still, watching Mydei expectantly. Only when his eyes drift to one of Mydei’s hands does the former crown prince realize that he’s waiting for him to lead him, just as he has been for the past two months.

It stirs some feelings in his heart, though not all of them are necessarily good, because while he is happy to be someone whom Phainon can rely on, he does want him to be able to go back to being able to stand on his own two feet. Before his thoughts can take a turn for the worse, Mydei quiets them.

That’s exactly what we’re working towards.

To that end, he will continue supporting Phainon with whatever he needs. Guiding him around is at least easy, and he’s gotten used to it by now, and it’s not like he’s opposed to being seen holding hands with Phainon anyway. So he indulges Phainon’s silent request, taking his hand and gently leading him out of the conference room.

Unfortunately, Mydei quickly realizes that he’s not the best when it comes to “making new memories.” The walk through Marmoreal Palace isn’t anything extraordinary, nor does it really differ from what they’ve been doing daily at this point. Of course, there are so many things other Mydei could have suggested if Phainon wasn’t as damaged as he is, but he doubts contests of strength, speed, or wit are suitable for him right now.

He sighs internally, glancing Phainon’s way. Normally, his boyfriend would shine in situations that require spontaneity, but as per the current norm, he is quiet—although, he does look particularly alert today, slowly looking around and taking in the sight of their surroundings. And as they pass by the baths on the way to the outside of Marmoreal Palace, Phainon pauses, staring.

It’s then that Mydei realizes that it’s been two months since Phainon had come to the baths. He has been making sure Phainon stays on top of personal hygiene and helps him whenever necessary, of course, but the fact that he hasn’t been able to participate in one of the most well-known aspects of Okheman culture must be saddening, especially given how eager he used to be to bathe with Mydei.

But…Phainon is slowly getting better. He’s been able to walk through Marmoreal Market without issue, even at its busiest. Surely, a bath wouldn’t hurt?

“Do you want to bathe here?” Mydei asks.

Phainon doesn’t answer, though from the look on his face, he seems to be pondering the answer. His eyes drift from the cold baths to the hot baths, where they linger.

Mydei turns his head, following Phainon’s gaze. “You want to take a hot bath?” His lips twitch into a crooked smirk as he remembers their competition here—it was the last one Mydei had participated in before leaving for Castrum Kremnos, so it remains particularly stark in his mind. “Are you sure? The last time we came here together, you were soundly thrashed by me.”

He says as much mostly to see how Phainon reacts to the reminder. Phainon takes their rivalry very seriously, and Mydei has always taken great pleasure in riling him up, a sentiment that the swordsman reciprocates. Of course, Mydei already knows that it’s too much to expect that he’ll be able to stoke Phainon’s competitive spirit with such a provocation, but there’s a small part of him that hopes that he’ll see some hint of the spark he used to have.

Instead, Phainon only stares at Mydei, bewildered.

“Thrashed…?” he repeats.

Mydei’s smile fades a little. “During our hot bath competition,” he says, trying to swallow the budding apprehension. “The one that you challenged me to.”

“Hot bath competition…” Phainon looks down, thinking. But after a while, his eyebrows furrow. “...Can’t remember.” When he looks up again and sees the way Mydei’s face falls, he adds, “...Sorry.”

“...It’s fine,” Mydei replies, forcing himself to keep his tone light. “It was a while ago already.”

Phainon falls silent again, looking a little sullen now, and Mydei doesn’t have to be a mind reader to guess that he’s in no mood to bathe anymore. Feeling a stab of guilt that his comment had brought down the atmosphere, he contemplates, trying to figure out what to do next, before he hears a long and drawn-out groan.

“Ughhh. This is hard to watch.”

Mydei’s head snaps up at the voice, his head turning. Eventually, he spots the “culprit” in a shadowy corner: Cipher, who’s leaning against the wall with her arms crossed, an unimpressed look on her face.

“Little prince, you really don’t know how to have fun, do you?”

He doesn’t have a retort for that. She’s not exactly wrong. Hephaestion, Perdikkas, Ptolemy, Leonnius, and Peucesta had been steadfast friends who had introduced him to the warmth of companionship, but they hadn’t exactly had the time to indulge in pastimes when much of their time in the wild was spent foraging for food or fighting for their lives. It was only after he had come to Okhema where he had been able to partake in more frivolous activities. In that sense, Phainon was his first introduction to anything “fun.” Seeing his lowered gaze, Cipher sighs.

“Oh well. I guess I have to do everything around here, don’t I?” She trots over, her eyes on Phainon, and when she gets close enough, she leans closer, her arms crossed. “Hey there, Deliverer boy. Do you know who I am?”

“Miss Cipher,” Phainon replies almost immediately.

“Wow~ To think that Amphoreus’ almighty saviour would see fit to remember a lowly thief like me! I’m flattered.” Satisfied, she moves back. “You know what, I’m in a good mood now, so why don’t you let your elder show you what a real good time looks like?”

Mydei stares at her, perplexed. “What are you…?”

“Hush, little prince. Just follow me, okay?” She turns around and begins walking. When Mydei and Phainon don’t follow right away, she glances over her shoulder. “You coming?”

Not really sure what to expect but seeing no harm in playing along, Mydei makes eye contact with Phainon before gently pulling him after him.

As it turns out, Cipher’s definition of a “good time” is a shopping trip.

With Mydei acting as both the pack mule and the wallet.

Phainon is penniless as usual, but even if he wasn’t, Mydei would never dream of taking his money while he barely has any agency. Still, he can’t help but throw skeptical glances Cipher’s way as the bags hooked around his arms grow in number and weight—filled with things that either briefly catch Phainon’s attention or that Cipher shoves into Mydei’s hands and insists that Phainon was looking at—somewhat disgruntled at the fact that she hasn’t paid a dime since they stepped into Marmoreal Market. Unfortunately for him, the thief either doesn’t notice or is willfully ignoring him, prompting Mydei to eventually clear his throat.

“You intended for this to be a good time for Phainon,” he starts. “Yet I’ve yet to see you contribute at all.”

“What, are you unhappy with the arrangement?” Cipher flashes him a smug, fanged grin. “You did say you owed me, so why not just consider this the chance to finally pay me back?”

When she puts it like that, Mydei can’t exactly argue. He had said something along those lines a few weeks ago. As long as Phainon isn't the one being taken advantage of, then he has no issue, but some doubt about Cipher’s intentions remain, especially when many of the things that he’s paid for don’t fall under the category of things that Phainon might be interested in.

“...Is this really for Phainon?” he asks after letting the doubt fester for a little longer.

“Hmm? Who else would it be for?”

You, maybe? Mydei wants to say, but he holds his tongue, instead focusing on the matter at hand. “The shops that you have led us to are not ones that Phainon would regularly go to.”

“Yeah, that’s ‘cause Princess Homebody and little Hyacine were the ones having him tag along to these stores. But he wasn’t aware of anything back then, so it’s not like he could’ve picked anything he liked.” She turns, flashing a peace sign at Mydei. “Well? Am I a considerate senior or what? Actually, you don’t have to answer that—I already know.”

Oh.

Right. Cipher had been watching over Phainon, Castorice, and Hyacine since they began their outings, even before Mydei regularly began joining —and long before Phainon’s first session. Which means that she’s essentially giving him another chance to catch up on some of the many things that he had missed out on while he had been in his vegetative state.

With that realization sinking in, Mydei decides to silence the rest of his complaints, at least, until Cipher speaks again.

“And if he ends up not wanting any of the stuff you bought for him, I’m always happy to take it off his hands~”

And there was the ulterior motive.

He sighs, ready to pull Phainon along to continue following Cipher, but he feels a tug of resistance. Pausing, he glances at the swordsman, who is turned towards a small stall selling antique jewelry. The store owner’s eyes light up seeing Phainon’s attention on his wares, and he waves the three of them over. Phainon answers the beckons without letting go of Mydei’s hand, and Mydei doesn’t fight the pull, heading over with him. Cipher also follows along curiously.

“Huh. I don’t think they ever went to this one,” she murmurs to Mydei. The former crown prince raises his eyebrows, scanning over the jewelry on display. Phainon isn’t usually one for accessories, so Mydei can only guess that he was attracted to the aged appearance of most of the pieces.

“Lord Phainon! What a joy to see you up and about!” the owner says, then nods towards Cipher and Mydei as well. “Lady Cipher, Lord Mydei, it’s good to see you two as well. Is there anything my humble shop can provide you with today?”

Phainon doesn’t answer verbally, but his eyes travel between the jewelry on display, finally settling on a pair of link bracelets. The chains are divided into eight distinct segments, each section sporting a metal setting bearing seven different-coloured gemstones—a colour that matches each Chrysos Heir, Mydei notices. The eighth and final stone is a clear gem, shimmering pure white in the light of the sun. The jewels on their own would be eye-catching, but all together, they create a rather garish combination.

Unfortunately, Phainon remains fixated on the bracelet, and the storekeeper leaps on the opportunity.

“You have good eyes, Lord Phainon! Although I cannot tell you the origin of this pair of bracelets, I can assure you that it is crafted from the highest-quality ores and the finest of gemstones. Both pieces are completely genuine, authenticated by yours truly!”

As Phainon continues staring, Cipher elbows Mydei lightly, a smirk on her face. “You know what to do, little prince.”

Mydei groans softly—those bracelets really do look awfully gaudy—then moves forward to retrieve the jewelry from the display and holds them out for the owner. “We’ll take these two.”

“Much obliged, Lord Mydei!”

After exchanging the appropriate amount of balance coins for the twin bracelets and stepping some distance away from the shop, Mydei turns to Phainon and gently nudges them into his hands. However, Phainon only stares at them blankly, and Mydei quickly realizes that he may need help putting them on. Taking one of the bracelets back, he undoes it, then slips it around Phainon’s left wrist before clasping it back together. But when he tries to do the same with the other one, Phainon withdraws his right hand, raising his head and watching Mydei expectantly. Seeing Mydei’s bewildered stare, Cipher rolls her eyes.

“Seems like he wants you to match with him, little prince.”

At that, Mydei internally grimaces. The bracelet is exactly the kind of thing he’d expect Phainon to like, but it’s too tacky for his own tastes, and it clashes terribly with the rest of his outfit, so he’s not too keen on wearing it. His unwillingness shows in his hesitation, making a face as he looks at the piece of jewelry.

“Not going to put it on?” He can hear Cipher snickering behind him. “You’ll make our poor little Deliverer boy so sad.”

…But even without her unhelpful reminder, rejecting Phainon’s request while he’s like this wouldn’t sit well with him. So in the end, Mydei gives in, pulling his gauntlet off and tucking it away, then clasping the remaining bracelet around his wrist. After he’s done, he holds out his arm so Phainon can see.

“There,” he says. “Satisfied?”

At first, Phainon doesn’t say anything. But his mouth curls upwards in the beginnings of a small, faint smile, and it suddenly hits Mydei—how much he has missed seeing his beloved laughing without a care in the world.

The rest of the day passes without incident. With Amphoreus’ day and night cycles restored, the sun naturally begins its gradual journey towards the horizon, and by the time the Action Hour draws to a close, the skies over Okhema are painted in orange hues.

In spite of his initial misgivings, Mydei deems it a productive day. Though Phainon has barely said a word and is now once again expressionless, his eyes seem a little brighter than before. He doesn’t need to voice anything for Mydei to recognize that he enjoyed himself during their outing.

“Before we ascended to divinity, you and I would sometimes share meals at this time,” Mydei says absentmindedly, then turns to Phainon. “Shall we find somewhere to eat? Just like old times.”

He can’t immediately tell whether Phainon remembers their routine or not, but either way, he seems receptive to the idea and nods. Mydei smiles.

But of course, he can’t forget about Cipher. She’s the reason he had been able to see Phainon’s smile, after all.

“Would you like to come with us?” he asks, fully intending to pay for her share of the meal as an extra show of gratitude for her efforts today. But to his surprise, when he glances over his shoulder, he finds that Cipher is already gone.

The Chrysos Heirs receive very few updates about Aedes Elysiae’s restoration at first. In the meantime, on Anaxa’s and Hyacine’s request, Dan Heng retrieves the data bank's files on the mara and the many curative methods that the Xianzhou natives have attempted in the past. Although none of them had been successful on actual mara-struck individuals, Anaxa reasons that they’re worth trying on Phainon, who hasn’t actually been afflicted with the Abundance. His modified treatments continue for some time, and according to the Grove duo and Sunday, he responds quite well.

Finally, two Amphorean weeks later, Dan Heng returns with news from the outside, and the Chrysos Heirs gather in the conference room once more.

“Aedes Elysiae should be restored soon,” Dan Heng begins. “However, there’s one issue that we believed we shouldn’t keep from you.”

Aglaea nods. “I appreciate your transparency. Please do continue.”

“About the people who once lived there…” Dan Heng pauses, his brows furrowed, trying to best convey his message. “We were told that it would be very difficult to restore them, since their data was corrupted by the black tide. It’s not impossible, but it’s not guaranteed either—and even if it was, it would take a much longer time than it will to restore Aedes Elysiae itself. The only way we could absolutely ensure that they all come back would be to start another cycle, but…”

He doesn’t have to continue for the implication to sink in—that starting a new cycle would effectively kill everyone. A grave atmosphere settles over the room, broken only by a hum from Anaxa.

“It makes sense. Living people are far more complex than inanimate objects and vegetation,” he muses.

“Yes… And the restoration process will be further complicated by the amount of time that’s passed on Amphoreus. The only reason we were able to bring you all back to life more easily was because you had only died recently,” Dan Heng says. “The same goes for everyone else who was restored.”

Mydei lowers his head slightly, a stormy look in his eyes. He had been wanting to inquire about Hephaestion and his other companions, perhaps even his mother, but hearing the news, he decides to put the thought aside for now.

“Hmm… But as long as we have Aedes Elysiae itself, that’s a start, right?” Cyrene pipes up. “I’m sure just seeing the environment will help Phainon a lot.”

“Hold on. Going home to a desolate village may do him more harm than good,” Anaxa says, his voice stern. “I’m sure I speak for mostly everyone when I say that people make up at least half the memories of a home. If Phainon returns to Aedes Elysiae only to find it devoid of his friends and family, it may only remind him more of what he’s lost.”

“But it won’t be devoid of his friends and family,” Cyrene replies, glancing around the room at everyone else. “Because we’ll all be there with him. Won’t we?”

It doesn’t take too long for her subtle suggestion to sink in. Tribbie is the one who lights up first.

“That’s true! Snowy won’t have time to feel lonely if we make it fun for him,” she says. “That’s part of what it means to make good memories with him, right?”

“You got it, Tribbie!”

“...Hm. That’s a reasonable enough idea, I suppose.” Anaxa nods, then glances down at Hyacine, who has been quietly standing beside him, a thoughtful look on her face. “Hyacine. Is there anything you want to add?”

“Oh, I was just thinking…” Hyacine raises her head to look at Anaxa. “One of the things that tormented Lord Phainon for so long was his inability to save anyone… That’s what he mentioned during his debate with the Council of Elders at Dawncloud, yes?”

“That’s correct. Specifically, he was forced to kill all of his kin, who had been turned into black tide monsters.”

Hyacine looks saddened at that, but quickly forces her pained expression down. “And as the Flame Reaver, he brought the black tide to Aedes Elysiae himself millions of times… With so many memories of him killing his loved ones with his own two hands, it’s no wonder he’s struggling so much.”

“But those are all things that we already know. What are you suggesting, Hyacine?”

Hyacine turns to regard everyone in the room. “Our original intention was to take Lord Phainon to Aedes Elysiae to help him heal in a place he loved. But what if we reframed it as some sort of…task for him?”

“A task?” Mydei asks. “What do you mean?”

“From what I can tell, Lord Phainon bases a lot of his own worth on what he can do for other people,” Hyacine continues. “It may seem counterintuitive to put him to work while he’s still recovering, but it’ll be more difficult trying to help him adjust his mindset with the state he’s currently in… So I thought we could try playing into it instead.”

“Now that you mention it, Sunday did say that Phainon occasionally shows some resistance to his tuning,” Dan Heng says. “He said that while he’s no mind reader, he can feel faint hints of certain sentiments within Phainon… Things like guilt and unworthiness—like he doesn’t deserve the care he’s getting. They seem to be the cause of most of his ‘dissonance.’”

“Right, Sunnie mentioned that to me and Professor Anaxa as well,” Hyacine says with a nod, then quickly continues speaking before Anaxa can correct her on his name. “That’s why, I think giving him a task would help him take the first step to overcoming those feelings.”

“You still haven’t mentioned what this task you’re thinking of is,” Anaxa says pointedly.

Hyacine smiles. “What if we had Lord Phainon participating directly in Aedes Elysiae’s restoration efforts himself?”

The room once again falls silent, pondering the abrupt suggestion. It’s Cyrene who speaks up first, her eyes bright with comprehension.

“Ohh, I get it!” she says gleefully. “You’re so smart, Hyacine!”

“Ehehe… I’m glad you think so, Renie.”

Anaxa is the next to voice his understanding. “Hmm… Yes, I can see where you’re going with this. This may also be helpful in addressing the ongoing issue of his self-perception…especially regarding his identities as both the Flame Reaver and a Lord Ravager.”

Hyacine nods again. “If we can show him that destruction isn’t the only thing he’s capable of, I feel like it’d help him a lot!” She turns to Dan Heng. “But that does mean we can’t restore Aedes Elysiae completely. Is it possible to remove the black tide’s corruption but leave some things broken that we can fix? Not so much that the entire village is still in ruins, but enough so that we’ll all have something to do, to show Lord Phainon that we’re all there with him and helping him.”

Dan Heng doesn’t answer right away, raising a hand to his chin in thought before nodding as well. “I think it’s doable. I’m not sure how it’d work, but I can’t see it being a particularly difficult task for the Genius Society. I’ll raise the idea with them. They should be open to it.”

Hyacine beams. “Great!”

With her hands at her mouth, Cyrene giggles happily. “I can tell that this will be a really good trip. I’m getting excited already!”

Feeling similarly hopeful sentiments, Mydei nods in silent agreement. And as the room becomes awash in the murmurs of trip planning, he glances over at Phainon, who has been standing quietly at the window the entire time, staring at the sky. Sensing Mydei’s eyes on him, Phainon turns around, tilting his head curiously.

Chapter Notes

March/Evernight is mentioned in this chapter, but I'm not really sure what's going on with her so I kept it mostly vague. I didn't want to exclude her though, because I really like the Traiblazer/Dan Heng/March/Sunday quartet, so I'm pushing my agenda... That said, nothing else is based on anything that was revealed in 3.5, as I had these ideas before the version update.

I found this chapter hard to write, so as a result, I'm not that confident in it 😔 But hopefully, it's at least enjoyable for readers!

A week later, the Chrysos Heirs receive word that Aedes Elysiae has been restored, and they disperse into smaller groups as the date of the trip steadily crawls closer. One chamber in Marmoreal Palace is bustling with activity as Tribbie, Trianne, and Trinnon begin packing for the journey.

“Teleslate, check! Photostone, check! Hm… Are we forgetting anything?” Tribbie hums, looking up at Aglaea, who is seated at her favourite table during a rare moment of leisure. “Agy, have you packed yet?”

“I have. And yourself, teacher?”

“Mmhm! We’re double- and triple-checking all of our bags so we don’t forget anything! Make sure you do the same!”

“I will. …Ah. You just reminded me. There is one matter of great importance I must attend to—and certainly one that I absolutely cannot forget.”

Tribbie tilts her head. “What is it, Agy?”

Aglaea turns to the shadows. “Cifera,” she calls softly. “I know you’re there. You cannot hide from the golden threads.”

The figure concealed in the darkness stiffens for a split second before sighing. Cipher emerges, her arms raised in a headrest—the very picture of nonchalance. “Spoilsport. Why do you keep those things up, anyway? It’s not like the Council of Elders is any threat these days.”

“Be that as it may, we still live in tumultuous times. For the sake of those who are still nursing their wounds, I cannot let my guard down.” Her eyes soften. “But that is not what I wish to discuss with you.”

“Well?” Cipher yawns and stretches. “Out with it, then.”

“Will you be coming with us to Aedes Elysiae?”

Still partially turned away, Cipher pauses mid-stretch. “Huh? Was I actually invited?”

“Anyone is free to come. I’m sure after all the help you have provided him from behind the scenes, Phainon would be pleased to see you there,” Aglaea replies, not overtly acknowledging the way Cipher tenses for a moment. “But to answer your question, I did want to specifically extend an invitation to you.”

“Hmm~” The thief hums, her tail swishing languidly. “You sure about that? Setting a street cat loose in an empty village… You may as well be asking for all of Aedes Elysiae to get looted!”

“If that is the price I must pay for you to accompany us, then so be it. I will be sure to reimburse Phainon and the rest of the villagers for their stolen belongings.”

Cipher blinks, her mouth ajar in surprise at Aglaea’s complete lack of hesitation. She watches the Goldweaver’s unchanging expression, as if trying to search for any sign of deception. When she doesn’t find any, she quickly slips back into her indifferent facade and shrugs.

“Ahhh well. How can I refuse such a generous opportunity?” she says with a snicker, then turns around with a nonchalant wave of her hand. “Fine.

Since you can’t bear to be without me for even a second, I’ll be there when the time comes. But don’t come looking for me until then!”

Having silently watched the exchange, Tribbie giggles as Cipher disappears into the shadows once again, taking note of the genuine smile spreading across her face as she does. “Ciphy is as dishonest with her feelings as ever.”

Aglaea smiles too, her sightless eyes lingering on the spot Cipher once stood. “She is… But I’m pleased that in these thousand years we’ve spent apart, she hasn’t changed.”

“Professor Anaxa, we’re—oh…!”

Hyacine nearly trips over a stack of books, but luckily, she’s steadied by Little Ica. Thanking her little companion, she glances around Anaxa’s office, dismayed at the mess. With tools, stray manuscripts, and opened storage boxes strewn all over the place, it looks like a freak squall had torn the room apart. “Goodness… What happened? It looks like a storm passed through here!”

Anaxa’s head pokes up from behind his desk, his hair and clothes disheveled. “There you are, Hyacine. I was looking for one of my scrolls for the trip. Also, call me Anaxagoras.”

“Did that really require overturning your entire office…?” Hyacine pauses. “Wait, did you say ‘the trip?’ You’re coming to Aedes Elysiae with us?”

“Yes…? Of course I am. Why wouldn’t I?”

“Erm… Aedes Elysiae sounds like it’s a little out of the way. The journey won’t be too hard on you?”

“Nonsense. Will we not be traveling there by dromas? Steeds of such gentle temperament will make for a smooth voyage.” Anaxa’s one good eye gleams with glee as he grins. “Not to mention… Once we arrive, the dromases will be able to frolic in the open fields. I rarely have the chance to see them outside of their enclosures… I am keen to observe how their behaviour changes with so much land around them.”

Hyacine exchanges a glance with Little Ica. “Same old Professor Anaxa,” she says with an exasperated smile. “But…even if you say that, you’re worried about Lord Phainon too, aren’t you? Or rather… You want to make sure you’re close to him just in case he relapses, or something else happens. Right?”

Anaxa doesn’t say anything at first, quietly bundling some scrolls together and slowly slipping them into the sack that lays open at his feet. “I won’t deny that that’s part of the reason.”

“Hehe… Since we’re going to the countryside, make sure you relax too, professor. You’ve been working harder than all of us to make sure Lord Phainon gets better.”

“Not quite true. You’ve contributed greatly as well, Hyacine,” Anaxa replies matter-of-factly, finally turning to face Hyacine. “In fact, I am confident when I say that Phainon would not have made as much progress as he did without your therapeutic treatments or the recreational activities you have been planning for him.”

Hyacine’s smile warms. “In that case, I hope this trip is fruitful for all of us!”

“Indeed.”

When Mydei and Phainon embark, the sun has only begun to rise over Okhema. Though the streets are quiet and empty, and there’s no chance of Phainon getting separated, Mydei leads him by the hand as usual. His new bracelet catches the limited light, sparkling in all colours of the rainbow; its twin is currently secured around Mydei’s belt. His excuse is that he always wants to remain battle-ready and that jewelry makes a poor substitute for his gauntlets, but the arrangement does also spare him the sight of the awful, gaudy thing. Luckily, Phainon doesn’t seem to mind as long as he’s wearing it somewhere on his person and he makes no protest.

They walk in silence until they come across the corner where Castorice arranged to meet up with them. She’s already waiting there when Mydei and Phainon approach, and upon seeing them, she waves to them before jogging over.

“Lord Mydei.” She smiles up at him, hesitating, but when Mydei lets go of Phainon’s hand and opens his arms for her, she eagerly hugs him. Once she’s satisfied, she lets go and turns to Phainon. “Lord Phainon.”

“Miss Castorice. Good morning,” Phainon says, and though there’s no smile visible on his face, it can be heard in his voice. “Nice to see you.”

Castorice’s visage brightens. She, like many of the others, has been religiously keeping up to date with Phainon’s progress and is well aware that he’s been improving, but she’s happy to see that he’s speaking more nonetheless. “It’s nice to see you too, Lord Phainon. May I embrace you as well, to commemorate our meeting today?”

Phainon tilts his head, not really understanding her question. But knowing his boyfriend would never protest to a hug from Castorice, Mydei speaks up. “Go ahead, Castorice.”

Encouraged by Mydei, for she can trust that he will always put Phainon’s comfort above everything else, Castorice hugs Phainon tightly. The former Deliverer stiffens a little in surprise, but he slowly relaxes, loosely putting his arms around her. He can’t seem to hold on too tightly, but Castorice doesn’t look like she minds.

“‘...You’re warm,’” Castorice murmurs, lingering for a little longer. “‘As warm as I imagined you to be.’ I wanted to say these words to you before, but you could not hear me… So I’m happy I have the chance to tell you now.” She looks up. “I can only hope that I can offer you the same warmth as well, Lord Phainon.”

Phainon blinks, a little confused, before nodding. “Miss Castorice. Is warm,” he agrees, and Castorice practically beams. Witnessing the both of them in such high spirits, Mydei can’t help but smile as they all make their way to the designated meeting place, where the other Chrysos Heirs and the Trailblazers are waiting.

The trip to Aedes Elysiae is slow and uneventful, but Mydei supposes that that’s for the best. With the pleasant weather and the gentle gait of the dromases, the journey is surprisingly relaxing. Beside him, Phainon has been lulled to sleep by the rhythmic movement of their steed, his head on Mydei’s shoulder. Around them, snippets of the conversations that the others are having drift by his ears.

“Ah, Professor Anaxa, don’t lean so far over the saddle! You can observe the dromases when we get to Aedes Elysiae!”

“Leave him, Hyacinthia. If he falls and cracks his skull, that would leave me with one less headache to deal with.”

“Oh? Still so eager to get rid of me, Lady Goldweaver? Why not finish the deed yourself, then?”

“Sunday, are you okay? You look so tense…”

“...I’m fine, Mr. Dan Heng. It’s just that Miss Cipher has been staring at me quite intently. I’m not sure why…”

“I mean… Name a cat that wouldn’t pounce on a bird.”

“Stelle…”

“Are you taking pictures already, Cas? We haven’t even gotten there yet!”

“But traveling with everyone like this is so fun… Lady March… Lady Evernight? She suggested that I take many pictures to preserve these memories.”

“Oh! Trianne remembers Cas saying that she didn’t have any pictures of her friends before. These can be your first ones!”

“Yes. These are fitting first photos, aren’t they?”

“You should make an album with all of the pictures later.”

“Ohh, good idea, Trinnon! Trianne wants to see the album too!”

“Hee hee… I’ll show you when I make it.”

It’s like a scene out of a pleasant dream, or maybe a happy fairytale. Banter between comrades and friends, laughter shared beneath the warm sun… Months ago, Mydei would have deemed this kind of future unattainable in this life. He never wants to grow too complacent, because peaceful days tend not to last for him, but he supposes there’s no harm in basking in the moment for now.

Some time passes before he feels Phainon stirring again, and as he rouses, he raises himself from Mydei’s side. Blinking the sleep away from his eyes, he seems to realize quickly that he’s not in a familiar environment and looks around, but relaxes immediately upon seeing Mydei watching him.

“Did you sleep well?” Mydei asks.

Phainon nods, then begins looking around again. “Where are we?”

Mydei had already told him of the excursion beforehand, but he knows Phainon still struggles to retain information in his damaged state, so he remains patient. “We’re going on a trip.”

“To where…?”

“You’ll see,” he says, repeating the answer he gave him that morning, and when he notices that the green of the meadows they’ve been passing by is slowly metamorphosing into the gold of wheat stalks, he smiles. “You’ll see very soon.”

Curiously, Phainon turns his head to follow Mydei’s gaze, and when he, too, sees the vast expanse of wheat fields in the distance, his eyes slowly widen. Seeing the gold reflected in his eyes, Mydei knows that Phainon recognizes exactly where he is.

The dromases slow to a stop, allowing their riders to disembark. Mydei gets off first to help Phainon down from the saddle, and together, they join the others. As the sight of the idyllic landscape spreads before them uninterrupted and the sweet scent of wheat permeates the warm breeze, Phainon falls completely still, as if in disbelief at what he perceives. The Chrysos Heirs and Trailblazers pause behind him, waiting, allowing him a moment to take everything in.

Then, Cyrene brushes past him, turning on her heel to face the group, her hands behind her back, her silhouette framed in gold.

“Welcome to Aedes Elysiae,” she says with a bright smile as her eyes drift over to Phainon. “Or, I guess I should say…

“Welcome home, Phainon.”

Without needing Mydei to lead him, Phainon takes a slow step forward. Then another. Then another, until he’s walked past Cyrene. He eventually reaches the apex of a small knoll overlooking the entire village, the emotions that he’s unable to show on his face visible in his eyes, still wide and staring, and in the way his knees nearly buckle under the weight of what he must be feeling. Mydei is at his side in an instant, steadying him with a firm but gentle grip on his arm—to make sure he doesn’t fall, but also to ground him, to remind him that this isn’t a dream, but reality.

He watches Phainon’s eyes move slowly around the wheat fields and the beaten paths, the broken carts and worn scarecrows and houses and sheds, all in varying states of disrepair, but not unsalvageable. When the remnants of life register, he seems to notice that the entire village is abandoned and, confused, he turns back to the others.

“Where is…everyone?”

Cyrene smiles knowingly as she walks up to his side, watching the tranquil fields. “They’re all very far away right now,” she says. “But don’t worry. They’re making their way back as we speak. It may take them some time to complete the journey… Maybe a really, really long time. But eventually, they’ll come home, just like you did.”

“Mom and Dad too?”

“Mmhm.”

“And Livia… And Piso… And Galba… And Ms. Pythias?”

“Everyone.” Cyrene allows a moment for it all to sink in before she continues. “But you know, no one has lived here for a while, so everything looks a little beaten up—and that’s no state to be in for a happy homecoming!” She looks up at him. “Since we got here first, why don’t we try fixing up what we can? That way, when everyone comes back, the village will be all ready for them! What do you think, Phainon?”

Phainon stares at her, almost as if unsure. “I…can help?”

“Of course you can! You and I both know our hometown the best, don’t we? It’ll be a lot of work for just the two of us...but luckily, we’ll have a lot of helping hands.” She leans to the side, peeking around Phainon at the group behind them. “Right, everyone?”

Phainon turns to regard the others as well, the uncertainty still in his eyes, but all he receives in return are smiles and nods—all affirming their willingness to lend a hand to him. Mydei raises his head, meeting Phainon’s gaze with his own.

“Where should we start?” he asks. Realizing he and the others have placed the reins in his hands and are waiting for his direction, Phainon turns back to the village, thinking.

“...The houses,” he finally says, his demeanor more confident than before. “So everyone can have a place, to call home again.”

Seeing Phainon willingly take the lead, the Chrysos Heirs and Trailblazers exchange smiles and get to work.

The once-dormant village soon comes alive with bustling activity, the sounds of hammering and sawing, and friendly chatter.

Unsurprisingly, repairing Aedes Elysiae is a time-consuming and laborious job, but working together, they make quick progress. It would be impossible for ordinary people to restore so many dwellings to working order within just the span of a day, but the Chrysos Heirs are hardly ordinary people— Cipher zips to and from Okhema, bringing whatever materials they can’t harvest from the nearby woods; Aglaea weaves her golden threads to act as scaffolding and temporary framework, and her Garmentmakers maneuver building materials into place with the direction of Tribbie, Trianne, and Trinnon; and Anaxa uses his alchemy to create miracles, restoring fixtures and structures that are beyond repair. Hyacine and Sunday remain on standby to tend to any bumps and scrapes that the others may acquire as they work, leaving Mydei, Phainon, Stelle, and Dan Heng to cover the manual labour—or so he had thought, until Castorice stuns everyone into silence by easily lifting a comically tall tower of wooden beams into her arms and carrying them to where they need to be.

“Well, she is one half of a Titan,” Anaxa reasons amidst the dumbstruck staring. “It shouldn’t be surprising.”

With Castorice happily taking over his tasks, Mydei finally has a chance to take a breather. He notices Stelle resting beneath the shade of a tree, wiping the sweat from her brow, and walks over.

“You didn’t have to come,” he says, “But thank you.”

After all, it had been made clear to the Nameless that they were not obligated to accompany the Chrysos Heirs to Aedes Elysiae—they had already aided enough in Phainon’s recovery, along with the rest of Amphoreus’ restoration, all beyond the realm of normal altruism, and most of the Chrysos Heirs agreed it would be unfair to ask them for more. Still, Stelle and the others had insisted on coming along anyway, claiming that doing so aligned with their definition of “Trailblazing,” but what sticks out in Mydei’s mind is the way Phainon had lit up upon seeing Stelle waiting with the others.

“Wow, you’re so polite now. Such a far cry from what you were like when we first met,” Stelle replies with a cheeky grin.

Mydei laughs through his nose, remembering those simpler times with fondness. “I had no means with which to appraise you back then. But you and your comrades have proven yourself time and time again to be strong and virtuous. You are worthy of respect.” He pauses, noticing a distinct lack of pink-haired girls by Stelle’s side. “By the way, where are Cyrene and your other friend?”

He’s still unsure as to whether that other pink-haired girl is called “March” or “Evernight”—he’s heard her being referred to as both names. Stelle doesn’t provide any clarification on that matter, simply shrugging. “I have no idea. They slipped away somewhere while we were working. Maybe they’re checking on the fairies in the Membrance Maze…or maybe they’re slacking off? I wouldn’t be surprised.” She looks up at Mydei. “How about Phainon? Where is he? It’s weird not seeing him with you.”

Now that she’s brought that to his attention, Mydei glances towards village square, and true enough, he doesn’t see Phainon there, even though he’d stick out like a sore thumb among the scenery with his garb. But before he can answer, Sunday and Hyacine approach, the latter speaking up.

“If you’re looking for Lord Phainon, he’s in the fields surrounding Aedes Elysiae. Professor Anaxa is teaching him how to apply alchemic wards that will protect the village even after we leave,” she explains.

“Wards?” Mydei quirks an eyebrow. “I know nothing of alchemy as a craft, but I would assume setting up wards would require some level of expertise?”

“Ehehe… That’s what I thought too. But it seems like Professor Anaxa accounted for that.” Hyacine’s eyes twinkle. “I was wondering why he packed so many scrolls when we wouldn’t be here for more than a few days, but then I realized that he probably wrote some equations on them to help make the wards easier to apply, even for someone who doesn’t have any knowledge of alchemy or…”

Or someone with impaired cognition, goes unsaid, but she doesn’t need to voice that for the rest of them to understand.

“I’m quite pleased to see that Mr. Phainon hasn’t shown any signs of distress,” Sunday adds. “Mr. Anaxagoras requested that I keep an eye on him just in case being in Aedes Elysiae triggers a resurgence of negative emotions or memories, but he seems to be doing fine. I can only conclude that Miss Hyacine’s idea of having him participate in the village’s restoration efforts must be helping him.”

Hyacine lets out a small sigh. “That’s good to hear. I knew we would be taking a bit of a risk bringing him out here, but it looks like things are turning out well.”

Mydei and Stelle exchange relieved smiles. Then, a fifth voice interrupts them as Trianne flutters overhead.

“Heyyy! There you are!” she calls. “Come join us! We’re all taking a break to eat!”

Eager to check in with the others, the four answer Trianne’s beckons, following her as she leads them back to the heart of Aedes Elysiae.

By the time they reach the center of the village, a small cooking pot and an open fire have already been set up, and the others have gathered around. Mydei had assumed that they were going to share some of the food that they had packed for the journey, but instead, what he finds is a pile of freshly caught fish, with Dan Heng standing right behind it. Stelle lets out a low whistle when she sees the sight. “Wow. Where’d you get all of that?”

“Dan Heng caught them all,” Aglaea explains. Behind her, Cipher is practically drooling as she stares ravenously at the fish. “Thanks to him, we will not have to draw from our supplies, although we were not lacking in them to begin with.”

“Wait… But did we even pack fishing rods? How’d he catch so many?”

Dan Heng opens his mouth, but it’s then that March (Evernight?) makes her presence known from behind him. “He decided to take a swim in the lake,” she says with a wily smile, making him start. “It seems like the water temperature was just right for him.”

The Archivist clears his throat loudly and turns his head away, looking a little embarrassed for some reason. “...We’ll need to cook all of it, though.”

At that, everyone turns to Mydei, staring at him imploringly. Sighing, but having anticipated it, he steps forward.

“Fine,” he grunts, removing his gauntlets. “But all of you will help me gut and clean them. We’ll complete the preparations more quickly that way.”

For a taste of Mydei’s cooking, everyone happily obliges, and soon, the village square is filled with the sound of sizzling and the fragrance of lightly seasoned grilled fish.

Unexpectedly, the comfortable atmosphere throws him back to a much more different time and place, yet one that was similarly filled with laughter and camaraderie. He had shared many a moment like this during that decade he spent wandering the wilds, and though those times had been far more uncertain and fraught with perils, he had never once feared for the future, for he knew he would always have his most trusted friends at his back.

No one will ever be able to replace Hephaestion, Perdikkas, Leonnius, Peucesta, and Ptolemy in his mind, but the Chrysos Heirs are his companions all the same, and their presence does mend the scars that those five had left behind.

Speaking of companions…

Noticing that Phainon is suspiciously absent, Mydei looks around the square, searching until he finds him sitting a short distance away from the group. As he recovered more, he had developed a tendency to separate himself from the others when given the opportunity, Mydei has noticed, but he doesn’t know whether it’s a product of him sitting through numerous meetings that he hadn’t been able to participate in or whether it’s out of lingering guilt from his memories as the Flame Reaver. Either way, it’s another thing that they’ll have to address and correct, and Mydei intends to do that right now, approaching him with two fish skewers in hand.

“Phainon.”

Phainon, who had been staring at his new bracelet, raises his head, watching Mydei curiously as the former crown prince sits down beside him. The swordsman once had a healthy appetite, but Mydei knows that nowadays, he won't eat unless prompted—not that either of them need sustenance to begin with—so he presses one of the skewers into his hands, then closes his fingers around it. “Eat.”

Phainon stares at the skewer for a few moments, then raises it to his lips, nibbling it. He seems to like it, so he takes a larger bite, and for a moment, Mydei can see more of his former self in his enthusiasm.

“Is it good?” he asks. Phainon nods, now focused on eating, and Mydei waits for him to finish before he starts talking again. “How are the repairs around Aedes Elysiae?”

“Going well,” Phainon replies. “Looks like how I remember… Wanted to stay, and wait for everyone to come back. But Professor Anaxa said no. I should go back to Okhema first. So he showed me how to use…" His eyebrows furrow as he fights to remember the word he wants. "Wards. They’ll keep the village safe, while we’re gone. Until everyone returns.”

It’s the most Phainon has spoken since his treatment began, so he must be in higher spirits. Even so, Mydei can detect a hint of melancholy in his voice, so he places a hand over his—a reminder that he isn’t alone anymore.

“We will wait together in Okhema,” he promises, squeezing Phainon’s hand. “And when your kin return, we will lead them back to your homeland side-by-side.”

Phainon raises his head again, staring at Mydei, his lips slightly parted in surprise. But he seems to have understood the vow, and he nods, and for the first time since he regained awareness, he squeezes Mydei’s hand in return.

Mydei would be content to spend the rest of their break like that, quietly resting, hand-in-hand. But then, a third voice rings out, interrupting their moment.

“Phainon!”

It’s Cyrene. At the sound of her voice, Phainon immediately raises his head, searching until he finds her waving to him from beneath a large tree. “Come help me out!”

He nods, standing up and walking over to her, and Mydei follows quietly, curious about what she would need help with. When they get to the tiny dock at the foot of the tree, he sees the wooden swing lying tangled amidst a loose coil of rope. It doesn’t seem to be broken otherwise, so it can be tied back onto the branch as is, but a task like that might be quite difficult for Cyrene, who’s quite diminutive in stature. It’s no surprise that she had called for Phainon.

“Lend me your muscles, will you?” she says. “The seat is heavier than it looks!”

Phainon nods again, kneeling down to pick up the wooden plank that serves as the seat and one of the ropes on the ground. However, he pauses after that, staring at the items in his hands without moving. Mydei quickly realizes that in his impaired state, Phainon may not know what to do to fix the swing, so he steps forward and touches his arm to get his attention, then picks up another length of rope.

“Just follow my lead.”

Phainon raises his head, watching as Mydei strings the rope through the hole in the seat, loops it, and ties it into a secure knot. Once Mydei is done, Phainon mimics him. He’s a little clumsier than usual, but Mydei can definitely see a shadow of his usual deftness in his movements—a sign that he’s getting better.

Once the swing has been reassembled, Mydei and Phainon work together to secure it to its usual branch. After ensuring it’s safe to sit on, the two stand back, watching it sway lazily in the wind.

Mydei nods at Cyrene. “It’s ready. You can sit on it now.”

Delighted, Cyrene trots over and sits down on the swing, then hums happily. “Mmhm~ Good work, you two! It’s just like the good old days. It’s almost like I’m reliving the past right now.”

At that, Mydei glances at Phainon, noticing the flicker of recognition in his eyes. The other man seems to be lost in reverie as he takes in the sight of Cyrene languidly swinging, humming a gentle melody as she does.

“Old days…” he murmurs, and Cyrene nods, smiling at the two.

“Yes. It’s thanks to you both. Thank you, Mydei! Thank you, Phainon!”

With your own hands, you were able to recreate what you once destroyed.

The message hidden behind Cyrene’s cheerful gratitude doesn’t escape Mydei. And judging from the look in Phainon’s eyes, the way they soften, he seems to have realized what Cyrene is saying as well.

“...Oracle cards,” he says after a brief moment of silence. Cyrene turns to him again.

“Do you want me to do a reading for you?”

Phainon nods, then quietly adds, “The old days. It reminded me.”

“Hehe~ Feeling nostalgic, are we? Let’s see what fate has in store for you today…" She pulls an odd-looking book out of her bag. "Come a little closer, you two. I’ll do a reading for the two of you together.”

Not knowing what to expect, Mydei follows Phainon, and the two of them sit by the swing to wait for Cyrene to finish her reading. He isn’t really sure what she’s doing, but after some time, she pulls two cards from her book.

“Here they are!”

She lays two cards before the two men, and both of them fall silent.

The first card reads “The Dawn.” It displays a colourful image of all the Chrysos Heirs and the Nameless joined hand-in-hand beneath a pale lilac sky. The Phainon depicted on the card seems to have a particularly bright smile on his face, enough to rival the rising sun behind him.

The second card is much simpler, depicting only Mydei and Phainon. In the image shown, the two are facing one another, one of their hands intertwined, the other raised to frame each other’s faces. Mydei feels heat spreading across his cheeks when he sees what the title of the card is.

The Lovers.

In contrast to Mydei, Phainon seems a little more clueless, just staring at the cards. It’s only when he hears Cyrene giggling that he raises his head.

“Wow~” Cyrene says. “Looks like you two have a joyous, romantic future waiting for you both! Lucky you!”

Mydei isn’t sure what to say to that. But Phainon is fixated on something else, watching Cyrene inquisitively. After gathering his thoughts, he speaks again.

“Felt different. The cards too.”

“Are you saying that my reading didn’t feel like how it usually does?” she asks, and when Phainon nods, she smiles coyly.

“Because it wasn’t an actual reading, Phainon.”

Phainon blinks at her inquisitively. Similarly confused, Mydei stares at Cyrene, silently demanding answers. For example, if this wasn’t a reading, where on earth had she gotten a card with him and Phainon, specifically, being so intimate with one another?

Perhaps…it was the “gift” that she mentioned not too long ago? The one that she said necessitated Stelle’s and March’s help? But how did they manage to procure something like this?

Amused at both of their expressions, Cyrene winks at Mydei, answering his silent inquiry with a look that very much says “It’s a secret.” Then, she reaches over and flicks Phainon lightly across the forehead. He flinches, recoiling slightly to rub the spot she flicked, now more confused than before.

Cyrene continues speaking, her light and airy tone befitting her youthful features, yet now carrying the weight of wisdom behind it.

“Readings are for people who are bound by fate,” she says. “But none of us are chained by fate anymore. We’re all free.

“And it’s all thanks to you, Phainon.”

She meets his eyes and smiles.

“You never gave up on the world we loved. Just like you promised me.”

Phainon falls silent, processing her words. There’s no indication of whether he fully understands them or not, or how much he actually remembers of the promise that Cyrene speaks of. But when he raises his head to look at Mydei, uncertainty in his eyes, Mydei nods, silently reinforcing Cyrene’s remark, encouraging him to take the first step forward into the future he had sacrificed himself endlessly for.

So you live freely too, Phainon. Live for yourself now.

Seeing Mydei’s encouragement, Phainon slowly reaches for the two cards, gingerly picking them up and holding them to his chest. A small, gentle smile spreads across his face, like a flower blooming after a long winter, tinted by the familiar warmth that Mydei has longed to see.

Chapter Notes

WE MADE IT...... What a journey it's been. To be honest, I lost confidence so many times while writing this fic because it turned out to be more of an undertaking than I thought it'd be. I actually didn't intend for it to be this long, nor was I thinking of going into so much detail about Phainon's recovery, and including all the Chrysos Heirs (sans Cerydra and Hyselins, since this fic was started before 3.5) was pretty challenging. I did really enjoy writing all the different character interactions, but this was definitely a lot more than what I planned to do with a little angst scenario I came up with on a whim. Hopefully the end result isn't disappointing!

Thank you to everyone for your support! It was fun reading everyone's comments and reactions to everything that happened, and seeing such positive reception was really motivating, even when I was at my lowest. And wow, I can't believe I've gone from writing a one-shot maybe once every six months to finishing multiple multi-chapter fics in not even a year... The power of Amphoreus is amazing...

Finally, I'm aware the CN MyPhai fandom has been reading this fic. Thank you so much for reading! I have a message for any CN readers who happen to be keeping up with updates on AO3 (thank you to Uryan for helping me translate!): 我知道有来自中国的敌厄同担在看 这篇同人文，而Uryan给我转发了很多你们的评论。所有的评论都 好温暖，而且它们让我更有信心去写完这篇文。谢谢你们这么享 受这篇故事！

Anyway, without further ado, here's the final chapter! It's more of an epilogue, so it's a bit shorter, but hopefully satisfying. Once again, thank you for sticking with me for this long!

With the collective efforts of the Chrysos Heirs and the Nameless, Aedes Elysiae is restored.

They spend the latter half of the last day of their trip enjoying the fruits of their labour, passing it in the peace of the sleepy village and the company of one another. When the sun sets, everyone gathers in the Sacrament Courtyard—their evening routine for the past few days—watching the stars on blankets and cushions that Cyrene had unearthed from her old storage chests. It’s warm enough to sleep outside, and one by one, they drift off under the curtain of the night sky and to the sound of comfortable chatter.

Outside of Okhema, Mydei always instinctively falls back on old habits, and he is among the last to fall asleep, remaining on high alert even long after everyone else has gone silent. However, the feeling of Phainon’s warm body in his arms, the sound of his soft breathing, and the gentle, rhythmic rise and fall of his chest eventually lulls Mydei into drowsiness as well, and he, too, drifts off.

When he awakes again, the sky is brighter, but the sun hasn’t yet risen. Still groggy, it takes him a few moments to remember that he’s currently in Aedes Elysiae—

—and for the empty space beside him to completely register.

Startled, he immediately sits up, his head swiveling to and fro. Judging from the colour of the sky, it's still very early in the morning, and everyone is still asleep, but Phainon is nowhere to be found—the swordsman has disappeared completely, as if he never existed in the first place.

Before he can lose himself to his irrational fears (why, why does an existence completely devoid of Phainon feel so strangely familiar, why does he feel so acquainted with the void that idea opens in his heart, as if he has experienced it before?), Mydei catches himself. The spot beside him is still warm, which means Phainon had only vacated it recently—and that means he couldn’t have gone far. With that in mind, the former crown prince calms down enough to feel disgruntled that Phainon hadn’t woken him up to accompany him, but he figures that it’s very like him to be so unnecessarily considerate.

Not wanting to wake his companions, Mydei slowly rises to his feet and carefully picks his way over the sleeping bundles scattered across the floor. Along with Hyacine, Castorice, Sunday, and Stelle, Mydei and Phainon had fallen asleep on the second floor of the courtyard, giving both of them access to the balcony. Mydei makes his way to the railing now, taking one look at it before vaulting over it, landing lightly on the ground outside the courtyard with barely a sound.

Save for the swaying of wheat stalks in the cool breeze, Aedes Elysiae is still and quiet. He figures Phainon should be easy to find, but even after scanning his surroundings, Mydei doesn’t see him in the immediate vicinity of the courtyard. So he takes a slow walk through the empty village, his eyes raking over everything for any sign of activity. He eventually finds them in the form of fresh footprints on one of the dirt paths, matching Phainon’s size perfectly. Following them, it doesn’t take that much longer for him to notice a figure sitting within the wheat stalks, nearly perfectly concealed, and he wastes no time in walking over. Mydei is normally as silent as a hunter, but this time, he makes sure his footfalls sound a little louder to make his approach known and avoid startling Phainon.

“Well, well, well. Awake so early? That’s a surprise. And here I thought you’d be impossible to drag out of bed,” he drawls.

Of course, that's blatantly untrue—during the old times, on their days off, Phainon was usually the one who was up and about first, provided he actually managed to fall asleep the night before. But after seeing him smile the other day, Mydei has really begun missing their banter and is filled with the urge to try taunting his lover a little.

Unfortunately but expectedly, Phainon doesn’t take the bait, simply looking up at Mydei with a vacant glance. “Mydei…”

Seeing that his provocations had flown over Phainon’s head, Mydei makes no further attempt to rile him up, simply crossing his arms and looking down at him sternly. “You should’ve woken me.”

“...Sorry. Wanted to see Aedes Elysiae, before we left. But everyone, seemed tired. Didn’t want to make noise."

Mydei supposes that’s reasonable enough, though he doubts that anyone would’ve woken anyway—everyone is quite fatigued from the labour they had been carrying out over the past few days, sleeping deeply through the nights. But before he can say anything more to admonish Phainon, the swordsman shuffles to the side, making some room for Mydei to sit. Recognizing the invitation to join him, Mydei obliges, sitting down beside Phainon. From where they are now, they have a perfect view of the glowing horizon, the sea reflecting the sky like a scintillating mirror.

“I remember. This spot,” Phainon says after a while. “It’s my favourite. Every time I’m born, in every cycle. Here, no one could find me, when I didn’t want to be found. No one but Big Snowy.”

A beat, before he turns to Mydei. “But you found me.”

“Because I will always find you.”

Just as Mydei had found Phainon in the failed Strife trial, and just as he had found him now, unearthing him from the grief and pain that had smothered him for an eternity.

“No matter how far away you are, no matter where you go,” he promises. “I will always find you.”

Phainon’s eyes soften. Mydei can’t tell whether he remembers the travails of the 33,550,336th cycle or not, but as long as he understands the depths of his fidelity, then that’s all that matters. Falling silent once again, the two continue watching as the horizon steadily grows brighter, daybreak approaching Aedes Elysiae.

“...Pretty,” Phainon murmurs after a few more moments of silence. “This sight… It’s so pretty.”

“Do you like it?” Mydei asks. When Phainon nods, he smiles, deciding that now is a good time to reinforce the message that all of the Chrysos Heirs had been trying to convey to him while trying to help him heal.

“This is the dawn that you ushered into Amphoreus, Phainon.”

“Wasn’t me,” Phainon replies almost immediately. “It was her. Stelle. The real hero. Her, and all of you.”

“But it’s because of your efforts that she was able to find us. Phainon… You are every bit as much of a hero as she is.” Mydei pauses, then adds, “Nothing less than the Deliverer spoken of in the prophecies.”

Phainon falls quiet, staring pensively at the stalks of wheat swaying in the breeze. Then, unexpectedly, he continues speaking again.

“I troubled, all of you,” he says quietly. “I caused so much pain. Again and again. Then, with Irontomb, at the end. I couldn’t stop it completely. And now… All this. This was for me too. Wasn’t it?” He looks down. “I’m sorry.”

Mydei stares at Phainon pensively, realizing what he's trying to say: that no hero would have to rely so much on others, or so Phainon thinks. With more awareness returning to him than ever, the guilt that Dan Heng had mentioned must be rearing its ugly head, but it’s also so like Phainon to beat himself up over the things he perceives to be burdens on other people. It almost throws Mydei back to the simpler times, when he would just smack Phainon upside the head with his palm and tell him to stop overthinking, but he remembers their circumstances and holds himself back. He probably shouldn’t hit Phainon’s head right now, since that’s where most of the damage is.

Instead, he settles for placing his hand on Phainon’s crown. Then, he pushes his head down, until the action earns him a confused whine and weak squirming. It’s a comical sight, and it makes Mydei smirk crookedly, both in amusement and silent gratitude that he can now enjoy such moments with his beloved after spending so long feeling like he would crumble to dust and ash at the slightest touch.

“Right now, your brain can barely hold enough words for you to string two complete sentences together. Instead of wasting your limited mental capacity on endless apologies, why don’t you spare room for a ‘thank you’ to everyone who’s helped you?” Mydei’s voice softens. “Is it so hard to fathom that they wanted you to recover? That you are cherished?”

Phainon pauses, tilting his head slowly until Mydei can see his blue eyes staring at him through the curtain of his white tresses.

“No matter what happened, what’s happening now, or what will happen… They will always love you,” Mydei continues, removing his hand from the top of Phainon’s head to cup his cheek instead, tilting his face up once again. “And I…

“I will always love you, Phainon.”

And Mydei knows Phainon understands him—that the love he speaks of is a different one from the others, equally enduring yet carrying the weight of unceasing devotion. Though Phainon’s expressions still lack most of their emotion, Mydei can see that recognition in the way his slightly widened eyes glisten, catching the first rays of light that emerge over the horizon. More sunbeams follow, illuminating the clear, pale skies and heralding the sun’s rise, but in spite of the breathtaking sight, Phainon’s gaze remains fixed on Mydei.

“Mydei… This whole time, you’ve been with me?”

“...Not the whole time,” Mydei admits guiltily. “But as much as I could.”

“...Were you sad?” Phainon pauses. “Did I…make you sad?”

Now it’s Mydei’s turn to fall silent. Yes, yes he had felt sad, anguished even. And he had felt helpless, agonizingly so. And he had felt anger, anger at the world that had forced Phainon to burn himself to cinders, anger at Phainon, who had sacrificed himself and was still so willing to sacrifice himself without consideration for those he would leave behind, but mostly, Mydei had felt anger at himself for his own ignorance, for not being able to prevent it all from happening in the first place, for allowing his beloved to suffer in silence and solitude for so long.

But he can’t convey all of that, and he has no desire to. He’ll have plenty of time to reconcile his own feelings once Phainon has recovered more, anyway. For now, he only reaches over, an arm settling around Phainon’s shoulders.

“...HKS. Stop wasting your breath asking me foolish questions. The only one you should be worrying about right now is yourself.” He pulls Phainon closer, keeping him within his grasp, as if the very action will prevent anything or anyone from ever taking him away again. “If you’re truly so concerned, then swear to me that you will stay by my side until you draw your last breath. That’s the only way you can make up for it.”

Phainon doesn’t respond.

Not at first.

But then, he finally nods, snuggling a little closer to Mydei, curling against him. It's all the swordsman can manage at the moment, but even so, Mydei can feel even more of his old self returning in the gesture.

“Mm. I’ll stay with you. Forever.” Phainon’s fingers loosely grip the fabric of Mydei’s half-robe. “Promise.”

“Idiot. Nothing lasts forever. But…it’s true that we both have a lot of time.”

Between his status as the Strife demigod and Phainon’s powers as both the demigod of Worldbearing and a Lord Ravager—whatever that entails—they could potentially have an eternity together. Mydei squeezes Phainon’s shoulder, allowing himself a moment to indulge in the thought.

“We will not waste a single second of it.”

That is Mydei’s promise, resolute, reassuring, and hearing it, Phainon nods again. He doesn’t say anything else, resting his head against the crook of Mydei’s neck, and Mydei allows the silence to blanket them, simply basking in the cool sea breeze and his beloved’s company.

Whether Phainon is able to fully recover from the ordeals he has been through remains to be seen. Somehow, Mydei doubts that he will come away from his suffering without many, many lasting scars. And once the Astral Express leaves Amphoreus, the Nameless will depart with it, and the Chrysos Heirs will no longer be able to ask them for their help. Perhaps Phainon may even regress without Sunday’s tuning to temper the extremes of his negative emotions, or Dan Heng’s endless repository of information on possible cures that exist across the sea of stars, or Stelle’s stalwart support, her willingness to drop everything to stand with her companions and be their strength.

But just as Phainon had vowed to be there for him, Mydei swears that he will remain by Phainon’s side, come what may. And he’s confident that the other Chrysos Heirs share similar sentiments—that they will never let Phainon be alone again.

There’s no telling what the future holds, but Mydei has never been one to dwell on what is to come. Instead, he is content to enjoy the feeling of Phainon by his side, the knowledge of the allies at his back, and the beginnings of their first real future, starting with the sight of this dawn.

A dawn with the sun.
